zh: 1. 哲学的兴起
en: 1. The Emergence of Philosophy

zh: 在开始之前，你可能会忍不住问：“那又怎样？”我们真的有必要费心研究科学和哲学这些复杂问题吗？对于这样的问题，有两种可能的回答。如果问题意在询问：我们是否需要了解这些内容才能处理日常生活事务，那么答案显然是否定的。但如果我们希望理性地理解我们所生活的世界，以及自然、社会和我们自身思维方式中起作用的基本过程，那么情况就截然不同了。
en: Before we start, you may be tempted to ask, “Well, what of it?” Is it really necessary for us to bother about complicated questions of science and philosophy? To such a question, two replies are possible. If what is meant is: do we need to know about such things in order to go about our daily life, then the answer is evidently no. But if we wish to gain a rational understanding of the world in which we live, and the fundamental processes at work in nature, society and our own way of thinking, then matters appear in quite a different light.

zh: 实际上，每个人都拥有一套“哲学”，因为哲学就是一种观察世界的方式。我们都认为自己懂得如何区分是非、善恶。然而，这些却是极其复杂的问题，历史上最伟大的思想家们都曾为此倾注心力。当面对伊拉克和阿富汗同胞相残的战争、大规模失业的重新出现，或叙利亚内战等可怕现实时，许多人会承认自己无法理解这些现象，并常常含糊地将其归咎于“人性”。但这种被视为万恶之源、且据称永恒不变的神秘“人性”究竟是什么？这是一个深刻的哲学问题，鲜有人敢妄加回答——除非他们具有宗教思维，那样的话，他们会说这是上帝以其智慧造就了我们。至于为何有人要崇拜一个对自己的造物耍这种花招的存在，那就另当别论了。
en: In reality, everyone has a ‘philosophy’, for a philosophy is a way of looking at the world. We all believe we know how to distinguish right from wrong, good from bad. These are, however, very complicated issues which have occupied the attention of the greatest minds in history. When confronted with the terrible fact of the existence of events like the fratricidal wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, the re-emergence of mass unemployment, or the civil war in Syria, many people will confess that they do not comprehend such things, and will frequently resort to vague references to ‘human nature’. But what is this mysterious human nature which is seen as the source of all our ills, and is alleged to be eternally unchangeable? This is a profoundly philosophical question, to which not many would venture a reply, unless they were of a religious cast of mind, in which case they would say that God, in His wisdom, made us like that. Why anyone should worship a Being that played such tricks on His creations is another matter.

zh: 那些顽固地坚持自己没有哲学观的人是错误的。据说，自然厌恶真空。那些缺乏一套系统完善的哲学立场的人，不可避免地会反映出他们所生活的社会和环境的观念与偏见。这意味着，在特定语境下，他们的脑海中充斥着从报纸、电视、布道坛和课堂上吸收的观念，而这些观念忠实地反映了现存资本主义社会的利益和道德观。
en: Those who stubbornly maintain that they have no philosophy are mistaken. Nature abhors a vacuum, it is said. Those who lack a coherently worked-out philosophical standpoint will inevitably reflect the ideas and prejudices of the society and the milieu in which they live. That means, in the given context, that their heads will be full of the ideas they imbibe from the newspapers, television, pulpit and schoolroom, which faithfully reflect the interests and morality of existing capitalist society.

zh: 大多数人通常在生活中浑浑噩噩地过日子，直到某种巨大的动荡迫使他们重新审视自己从小接受的思想和价值观。社会的危机迫使他们对许多曾视为理所当然的事情提出质疑。在这样的时刻，那些看似遥远的思想突然变得格外切合实际。任何希望理解生活——而非将其视为一系列毫无意义的偶然事件或不假思索的例行公事——的人，都必须投身于哲学，即超越日常生活中眼前的问题，进行更高层次的思考。唯有通过这种方式，我们才能提升自己，达到一个新的高度，从而开始发挥作为有意识的人的潜能，既愿意也能够掌控自己的命运。
en: Most people usually muddle through life until some great upheaval compels them to reconsider the kind of ideas and values they grew up with. The crisis of society forces them to question many things they took for granted. At such times, ideas which seemed remote suddenly become strikingly relevant. Anyone who wishes to understand life, not as a meaningless series of accidents or an unthinking routine, must occupy themselves with philosophy, that is, with thought at a higher level than the immediate problems of everyday existence. Only by this means do we raise ourselves to a height where we begin to fulfil our potential as conscious human beings, willing and able to take control of our own destinies.

zh: 人们普遍认为，生活中任何有价值的事物都需要付出一定的努力。哲学研究因其本质而涉及某些困难，因为它所探讨的问题远离普通经验的世界。就连所使用的术语也会带来困难，因为词语的用法未必与日常惯用语相符。但从工程学到心理学，任何专业学科都是如此。
en: It is generally understood that anything worthwhile in life requires some effort. The study of philosophy, by its very nature, involves certain difficulties, because it deals with matters far removed from the world of ordinary experience. Even the terminology used presents difficulties because words are used in a way which does not necessarily correspond to the common usage. But the same is true for any specialised subject, from engineering to psychology.

zh: 第二个障碍更为严峻。如前所述，在十九世纪，当马克思和恩格斯首次发表关于辩证唯物主义的著作时，他们可以假设许多读者至少对古典哲学（包括黑格尔的思想）具备基础了解。如今，我们已无法再作此种假设。哲学不再占据以往的地位，因为关于宇宙和生命本质的思辨早已被科学所取代。凭借强大的射电望远镜和航天器，我们已无需再对太阳系的性质和范围进行猜测。就连人类灵魂的奥秘，也正随着神经生物学和心理学的进步而逐渐被揭示。
en: The second obstacle is more serious. As has been explained, in the nineteenth century, when Marx and Engels first published their writings on dialectical materialism, they could assume that many of their readers had at least a working knowledge of classical philosophy, including the ideas of Hegel. Nowadays, it is not possible to make such an assumption. Philosophy no longer occupies the place it had before, since the role of speculation about the nature of the universe and life has long since been occupied by the sciences. The possession of powerful radio telescopes and spacecraft renders guesses about the nature and extent of our solar system unnecessary. Even the mysteries of the human soul are being gradually laid bare by the progress of neurobiology and psychology.

zh: 在社会科学领域，情况则远不如人意，这主要是因为当科学触及支配人们生活的强大物质利益时，人们对准确知识的渴望往往就会随之减弱。马克思和恩格斯在社会历史分析和经济学领域取得的巨大成就，超出了本书的讨论范围。只需指出：尽管马克思主义的社会理论自诞生之初就遭受了持续且往往恶意的攻击，但它们仍是现代社会科学发展的决定性因素。这些思想的活力体现在：针对它们的攻击不仅持续存在，而且随着时间的推移，其强度甚至有增无减。
en: The situation is far less satisfactory in the realm of the social sciences, mainly because the desire for accurate knowledge often decreases to the degree that science impinges on the powerful material interests which govern the lives of people. The great advances made by Marx and Engels in the sphere of social and historical analysis and economics fall outside the scope of this present work. Suffice it to point out that, despite the sustained and frequently malicious attacks to which they were subjected from the beginning, the theories of Marxism in the social sphere have been the decisive factor in the development of modern social sciences. The vitality of these ideas is testified to by the fact that the attacks not only continue, but tend to increase in intensity as time goes by.

zh: 在过去的时代，科学的发展——它始终与生产力的发展紧密相连——尚未达到足够高的水平，无法让人类理解他们所生活的世界。在缺乏科学知识或获取科学知识的物质手段的情况下，他们不得不依靠自己所拥有的唯一能够帮助他们理解世界、从而获得支配世界的力量的工具——人类的头脑。理解世界的斗争，与人类挣脱单纯动物性生存状态、驾驭自然的盲目力量、并在实际意义上（而非法律形式的意义上）获得自由的斗争紧密相连。这一斗争是一条贯穿整个人类历史的主线。
en: In past ages, the development of science, which has always been closely linked to that of the productive forces, had not reached a sufficiently high level to permit men and women to understand the world in which they lived. In the absence of scientific knowledge, or the material means of obtaining it, they were compelled to rely upon the one instrument they possessed that could help them to make sense of the world, and thus gain power over it – the human mind. The struggle to understand the world was closely identified with humankind’s struggle to tear itself away from a mere animal level of existence, to gain mastery over the blind forces of nature, and to become free in the real, rather than legalistic, sense of the word. This struggle is a thread running through the whole of human history.

zh: 宗教的作用
en: ROLE OF RELIGION

zh: 人类简直疯了。他连一只蛆都造不出来，却能成批地创造神明。
en: Man is quite insane. He wouldn’t know how to create a maggot, and he creates Gods by the dozen.

zh: 所有神话都在想象之中、通过想象来克服、支配并塑造自然之力；因此，随着人类真正掌握自然力量的到来，神话便随之消逝。
en: All mythology overcomes and dominates and shapes the force of nature in the imagination and by the imagination; it therefore vanishes with the advent of real mastery over them.

zh: 动物没有宗教，过去人们曾说，这正是人类与“野兽”的主要区别。但这只不过是另一种说法，即只有人类才拥有真正意义上的意识。近年来，针对“人类是特殊而独特的造物”这一观念，出现了一种反对意见。从人类源于动物，且在许多重要方面仍属动物这一意义上讲，这种观点无疑是正确的。我们不仅与其他动物共享许多生理功能，而且人类与黑猩猩之间的基因差异还不到2%。这对创世论者的无稽之谈给出了驳斥性的回答。
en: Animals have no religion, and in the past it was said that this constituted the main difference between humans and ‘brutes’. But that is just another way of saying that only humans possess consciousness in the full sense of the word. In recent years, there has been a reaction against the idea of humanity as a special and unique Creation. This is undoubtedly correct, in the sense that humans developed from animals and, in many important respects, remain animals. Not only do we share many of the bodily functions with other animals, but the genetic difference between humans and chimpanzees is less than 2 per cent. That is a crushing answer to the nonsense of the Creationists.

zh: 最近对倭黑猩猩的研究已无可置疑地证明，与人类最接近的灵长类动物在某些方面能够表现出与人类儿童相似的心理活动水平。这是人类与高等灵长类动物之间亲缘关系的惊人证明，但类比到此便开始失效。尽管科学家们付出了种种努力，圈养的倭黑猩猩仍无法说话，也无法制作出哪怕是与早期人科动物所创造的最简单工具相似的石器。人类与猿类之间2% 的基因差异，标志着从动物到人类的质的飞跃。这一飞跃并非由“造物主”完成，而是通过体力劳动推动大脑发展而实现的。
en: Recent research with bonobo apes has proven beyond doubt that the primates closest to humans are capable of a level of mental activity similar, in some respects, to that of a human child. That is striking proof of the kinship between humans and the highest primates, but here the analogy begins to break down. Despite all the efforts of scientists, captive bonobos have not been able to speak or fashion a stone tool remotely similar to the simplest implements created by early hominids. The 2 per cent genetic difference between humans and apes marks the qualitative leap from the animal to the human. This was accomplished, not by a Creator, but by the development of the brain through manual labour.

zh: 即使是制作最简单的石器，也需要极高的智力水平和抽象思维能力。能够挑选合适的石料并排除其他石料；选择正确的打击角度，并施加恰到好处的力道——这些都是极其复杂的智力活动。它们蕴含着一种连最先进的灵长类动物都不具备的规划能力和预见性。然而，石器的使用与制造并非有意识规划的结果，而是人类远古祖先在生存必要性驱使下被迫采取的行动。创造人类的并非意识，而是人类生存的必要条件——正是这些条件促成了大脑体积的增大、语言的产生以及包括宗教在内的文化发展。
en: The skill to make even the simplest stone tools involves a very high level of mental ability and abstract thought. The ability to select the right sort of stone and reject others; the choice of the correct angle to strike a blow, and the use of precisely the right amount of force – these are highly complicated intellectual actions. They imply a degree of planning and foresight not found in even the most advanced primates. However, the use and manufacture of stone tools was not the result of conscious planning, but was something forced upon man’s remote ancestors by necessity. It was not consciousness that created humanity, but the necessary conditions of human existence which led to an enlarged brain, speech and culture, including religion.

zh: 理解世界的需要与生存的需要紧密相连。那些最早发现利用石刮器处理皮厚的动物的尸体的人类祖先，相较于无法获取这种丰富脂肪和蛋白质资源的同类，获得了显著的优势。那些完善了石器制作技术、并摸清了最佳材料产地的人，比那些没有做到的人拥有更大的生存机会。随着技术的进步，思维也随之发展，同时产生了解释支配他们生活的自然现象的必要性。在数百万年的时间里，通过反复试错，我们的祖先开始建立事物之间的某些联系。他们开始进行抽象思维，即从经验和实践中进行概括。
en: The need to understand the world was closely linked to the need to survive. Those early hominids who discovered the use of stone scrapers in butchering dead animals with thick hides got a considerable advantage over those who were denied access to this rich supply of fats and proteins. Those who perfected their stone implements, and worked out where to find the best materials stood a better chance of survival than those who did not. With the development of technique came the development of the mind, and the need to explain the phenomena of nature which governed their lives. Over millions of years, through trial and error, our ancestors began to establish certain relations between things. They began to make abstractions, that is, to generalise from experience and practice.

zh: 几个世纪以来，哲学的核心问题一直是思维与存在的关系。大多数人过着相当幸福的生活，甚至从未考虑过这个问题。他们思考、行动、交谈和工作，都毫无困难。此外，他们根本不会认为这两种最基本的人类活动是相互矛盾的——实际上，这两者是密不可分的。即使最基础的行动——如果我们排除单纯由生物机制决定的反应——也需要一定程度的思考。在某种程度上，这不仅适用于人类，也适用于动物，观察一只猫潜伏等待捕鼠的情景便可看出这一点。然而，人类的这种思考和规划在质上远高于任何灵长类动物（即使是最高等的猿类）的任何精神活动。
en: For centuries, the central question of philosophy has been the relation of thinking to being. Most people live their lives quite happily without even considering this problem. They think and act, talk and work, with not the slightest difficulty. Moreover, it would not occur to them to regard as incompatible the two most basic human activities, which are, in practice, inseparably linked. Even the most elementary action, if we exclude simple biologically determined reactions, demands a degree of thought. To a degree, this is true not only of humans but also of animals, as can be seen when watching a cat lying in wait for a mouse. In man, however, the kind of thought and planning has a qualitatively higher character than any of the mental activities of even the most advanced of the apes.

zh: 这一事实与抽象思维能力密不可分，正是这种能力使人类能够远远超越感官所呈现的当下情境。我们不仅能设想过去的情境（动物也有记忆，比如看到棍子就畏缩的狗），还能设想未来的情境。我们能够预见复杂的情况，进行规划，从而决定结果，并在一定程度上决定自己的命运。
en: This fact is inseparably linked to the capacity for abstract thought, which enables humans to go far beyond the immediate situation given to us by our senses. We can envisage situations, not just in the past (animals also have memory, as a dog which cowers at the sight of a stick) but also the future. We can anticipate complex situations, plan, and thereby determine the outcome, and, to some extent, determine our own destinies.

zh: 尽管我们通常不会去思考这一点，但这代表着一项巨大的成就，使人类从自然界中脱颖而出。著名史前史学家戈登·柴尔德教授指出：“人类推理的独特之处在于，它能够从实际的当下情境中走得比任何其他动物的推理似乎所能达到的距离要远得多。”
正是这种能力孕育了文明、文化、艺术、音乐、文学、科学、哲学和宗教等丰富多彩的创造。我们也理所当然地认为，这一切并非从天而降，而是数百万年发展的产物。
en: Although we do not normally think about it, this represents a colossal conquest which sets humankind apart from the rest of nature. “What is distinctive of human reasoning”, says the celebrated prehistorian Professor Gordon Childe, “is that it can go immensely farther from the actual present situation than any other animal’s reasoning ever seems to get it”.

From this capacity springs all the manifold creations of civilisation, culture, art, music, literature, science, philosophy and religion. We also take for granted that all this does not drop from the skies, but is the product of millions of years of development.

zh: 古希腊哲学家阿那克萨戈拉曾通过精妙的推论指出，人类的智力发展取决于双手的解放。恩格斯在其重要文章《劳动在从猿到人的过渡中所起的作用》中，阐明了这一过渡的具体实现过程。他证明，直立行走——它使双手得以解放用于劳动——以及手部形态——特别是拇指与其余手指相对、从而能够抓握——正是制造工具的生理先决条件，而制造工具反过来又成为大脑发展的主要刺激因素。语言本身——它与思想密不可分——源于社会生产的需求，源于通过合作实现复杂功能的需要。恩格斯的这些理论得到了古生物学最新发现的有力证实，这些发现表明，人科猿类出现在非洲的时间远早于此前认为的，而且它们的大脑体积并不比现代黑猩猩的大。也就是说，大脑的发展发生在工具制造之后，并且是工具制造的结果。因此，“起初有道”这一说法并不正确，而是正如德国诗人歌德所宣称的那样：“起初有行动。”
en: The Greek philosopher Anaxagoras, in a brilliant deduction, said that man’s mental development depended upon the freeing of the hands. In his important article, ‘The Part Played by Labour in the Transition from Ape to Man’, Engels showed the exact way in which this transition was achieved. He proved that the upright stance, which freed the hands for labour, and the form of the hands – with the opposition of the thumb to the fingers, which allowed for clutching – were the physiological preconditions for toolmaking, which, in turn, was the main stimulus to the development of the brain. Speech itself – which is inseparable from thought – arose out of the demands of social production, the need to realise complicated functions by means of co-operation. These theories of Engels have been strikingly confirmed by the most recent discoveries of palaeontology, which show that hominid apes appeared in Africa far earlier than previously thought, and that they had brains no bigger than those of a modern chimpanzee. That is to say, the development of the brain came after the production of tools, and as a result of it. Thus, it is not true that “In the beginning was the Word”, but, as the German poet Goethe proclaimed: “In the beginning was the Deed.”

zh: 抽象思维能力与语言密不可分。戈登·柴尔德指出：
en: The ability to engage in abstract thought is inseparable from language. Gordon Childe observes:

zh: 推理，以及我们所称的一切思考活动——包括黑猩猩的思考——都必须涉及对心理学家所称的“意象”进行的心理运算。视觉意象——例如对一根香蕉的心理图景——往往只是特定环境中某根特定香蕉的画面。相反，正如前文所述，词语则更为普遍和抽象，它恰恰排除了那些赋予任何真实香蕉以个体性的偶然特征。词语的心理意象（即发音时所涉及的声音或肌肉运动的图景）构成了思考时非常便利的工具。借助它们进行的思考必然具备那种抽象性和普遍性，而动物的思考似乎恰恰缺乏这一点。人类不仅能谈论，还能思考被称为“香蕉”的物体类别；而黑猩猩的思考却永远停留在“那个管子里的那根香蕉”的层面。由此可见，被称为语言的社会工具，促成了那个被冠以宏大名称的过程——“人类从具体事物的束缚中解放出来”。
en: Reasoning, and all that we call thinking, including the chimpanzee’s, must involve mental operations with what psychologists call images. A visual image, a mental picture of, say, a banana, is always liable to be a picture of a particular banana in a particular setting. A word on the contrary is, as explained, more general and abstract, having eliminated just those accidental features that give individuality to any real banana. Mental images of words (pictures of the sound or of the muscular movements entailed in uttering it) form very convenient counters for thinking with. Thinking with their aid necessarily possesses just that quality of abstractness and generality that animal thinking seems to lack. Men can think, as well as talk, about the class of objects called ‘bananas’; the chimpanzee never gets further than ‘that banana in that tube’. In this way the social instrument termed language has contributed to what is grandiloquently described as “man’s emancipation from bondage to the concrete”.

zh: 早期人类经过漫长的时间，形成了对植物或动物等事物的普遍观念。这种观念源于对许多具体植物和动物的具体观察。但当我们得出“植物”这一普遍概念时，我们眼前看到的已不再是某一朵花或某一丛灌木，而是它们所共有的本质。我们把握的是植物的本质，即其最深层的内在本质。相比之下，个别植物的特殊特征显得次要且不稳定。永恒而普遍的特质蕴含在一般概念之中。我们实际上永远看不到一种与具体花朵或灌木相区别的“植物本身”。它是一种思维的抽象。然而，当剥离所有次要特征后，它却是对植物本质的更深刻、更真实的表达。
en: Early humans, after a long period of time, formed the general idea of, say, a plant or an animal. This arose out of the concrete observation of many particular plants and animals. But when we arrive at the general concept ‘plant’, we no longer see before us this or that flower or bush, but that which is common to all of them. We grasp the essence of a plant, its innermost being. Compared with this, the peculiar features of individual plants seem secondary and unstable. What is permanent and universal is contained in the general conception. We can never actually see a plant as such, as opposed to particular flowers and bushes. It is an abstraction of the mind. Yet it is a deeper and truer expression of what is essential to the plant’s nature, when stripped of all secondary features.

zh: 不过，早期人类的抽象概念远未具备科学性质。它们只是试探性的探索，如同孩童的印象、猜测和假设，有时虽不准确，却总是大胆而富有想象力。对早期人类而言，太阳是一个伟大的存在，有时温暖他们，有时灼伤他们；大地是一个沉睡的巨人；火则是一头凶猛的野兽，一旦触碰便会咬伤他们。
en: However, the abstractions of early humans were far from having a scientific character. They were tentative explorations, like the impressions of a child, guesses and hypotheses, sometimes incorrect, but always bold and imaginative. To early humans, the sun was a great being that sometimes warmed them, and sometimes burnt them. The earth was a sleeping giant. Fire was a fierce animal that bit them when they touched it.

zh: 早期人类曾亲历雷电现象。这必然令他们感到恐惧，正如今天它依然令动物和人类感到恐惧一样。但与动物不同，人类试图为这一现象寻找一个普遍的解释。鉴于缺乏任何科学知识，这种解释无一例外都是超自然的——某个神明正用锤子敲击砧铁。在我们看来，这样的解释似乎只是可笑的，就像孩子天真的解释一样。尽管如此，在那个时期，它们却是极其重要的假说——这是人们试图为这一现象寻找理性原因，在此过程中，人们把直接经验与某种完全不同于它的东西区分开来，并认识到后者。
en: Early humans experienced the phenomenon of thunder and lightning. This must have frightened them, as it still frightens animals and people today. But, unlike animals, humans looked for a general explanation of the phenomenon. Given the lack of any scientific knowledge, the explanation was invariably a supernatural one – some god, hitting an anvil with his hammer. To our eyes, such explanations seem merely amusing, like the naive explanations of children. Nevertheless, at this period they were extremely important hypotheses – an attempt to find a rational cause for the phenomenon, in which men distinguished between the immediate experience, and saw something entirely separate from it.

zh: 早期宗教最典型的形式是万物有灵论——即认为一切事物，无论是有生命的还是无生命的，都拥有灵魂。当孩子撞到桌子后，又拍打那张桌子时，我们也能看到类似的反应。同样地，早期人类以及当今某些部落，在砍伐一棵树之前，会先请求树的灵魂原谅他们。万物有灵论属于人类尚未完全脱离动物世界及自然界整体的时期。人类与动物世界的亲近关系，从洞穴艺术的鲜活与美感中可见一斑——其中的马、鹿和野牛被描绘得如此自然，这种自然感是现代艺术家再也无法捕捉的。那是人类种族的童年时代，如今已经一去不复返。我们只能想象这些遥远的祖先的心理状态。但通过将考古学与人类学的发现相结合，我们至少可以大致重构出我们所诞生的那个世界。
en: The most characteristic form of early religion is animism – the notion that everything, animate or inanimate has a spirit. We see the same kind of reaction in a child when it smacks a table against which it has banged its head. In the same way, early humans, and certain tribes today, will ask the spirit of a tree to forgive them before cutting it down. Animism belongs to a period when humankind has not yet fully separated itself from the animal world and nature in general. The closeness of humans to the world of animals is attested to by the freshness and beauty of cave art, where horses, deer and bison are depicted with a naturalness which can no longer be captured by the modern artist. It is the childhood of the human race, which has gone beyond recall. We can only imagine the psychology of these distant ancestors of ours. But by combining the discoveries of archaeology with anthropology, it is possible to reconstruct, at least in outline, the world from which we have emerged.

zh: 詹姆斯·弗雷泽爵士在其关于巫术与宗教起源的经典人类学研究中写道：
en: In his classic anthropological study of the origins of magic and religion, Sir James Frazer writes:

zh: 野蛮人几乎无法理解更先进民族通常所划分的自然与超自然之间的区别。对他而言，世界在很大程度上是由超自然力量所支配的，即由一些具有人格的实体所支配，它们像他一样受冲动和动机驱使，也像他一样容易被诉诸其怜悯、希望和恐惧的呼吁所打动。在这样构想的世界里，他认为这种为了自身利益而影响自然进程的力量是无穷无尽的。祈祷、许诺或威胁都可能使他从诸神那里获得晴好天气和丰收；而如果某位神灵——正如他有时所相信的那样——恰好化身为他自己，那么他就无需向更高层的存在祈求；他——这位野蛮人——自身便拥有促进自身及同胞福祉所需的一切力量。
en: A savage hardly conceives the distinction commonly drawn by more advanced peoples between the natural and the supernatural. To him the world is to a great extent worked by supernatural agents, that is, by personal beings acting on impulses and motives like his own, liable like him to be moved by appeals to their pity, their hope, and their fears. In a world so conceived he sees no limit to this power of influencing the course of nature to his own advantage. Prayers, promises, or threats may secure him fine weather and an abundant crop from the gods; and if a god should happen, as he sometimes believes, to become incarnate in his own person, then he need appeal to no higher being; he, the savage, possesses in himself all the powers necessary to further his own well-being and that of his fellow-men.

zh: 灵魂独立于身体之外存在的观念，可追溯至最遥远的野蛮时期。其依据十分明确：当我们入睡时，灵魂似乎会离开身体，在梦中四处游荡。由此延伸，死亡与睡眠之间的相似性（正如莎士比亚所言，睡眠是“死亡的另一个自身”），让人产生了灵魂在死后仍能继续存在的想法。因此，早期人类得出结论：体内存在某种与身体分离的东西。这就是灵魂，它支配着身体，即使在身体沉睡时，也能完成各种不可思议的事情。他们还注意到智慧之言常从老人口中说出，于是推断：身体虽会消亡，灵魂却继续存在。对于习惯于“迁徙”这一概念的人来说，死亡被视为灵魂的迁徙，而灵魂需要食物和器具来完成这段旅程。
en: The notion that the soul exists separate and apart from the body comes down from the most remote period of savagery. The basis of it is quite clear. When we are asleep, the soul appears to leave the body and roam about in dreams. By extension, the similarity between death and sleep (“death’s second self”, as Shakespeare expressed it) suggested the idea that the soul could continue to exist after death. Early humans thus concluded that there is something inside them that is separate from their bodies. This is the soul, which commands the body, and can do all kinds of incredible things, even when the body is asleep. They also noticed how words of wisdom issued from the mouths of old people, and concluded that, whereas the body perishes, the soul lives on. To people used to the idea of migration, death was seen as the migration of the soul, which needed food and implements for the journey.

zh: 起初，这些灵魂没有固定的居所。它们只是四处游荡，通常会制造麻烦，这迫使生者不惜一切代价来安抚它们。宗教仪式的起源便源于此。最终，人们产生了一种观念：可以通过祈祷来寻求这些灵体的帮助。在这个阶段，宗教（巫术）、艺术和科学尚未区分开来。由于缺乏真正掌控环境的能力，早期人类试图通过与自然进行巫术交往来达到目的，从而使自然服从于他们的意志。
en: At first these spirits had no fixed abode. They merely wandered about, usually making trouble, which obliged the living to go to extraordinary lengths to appease them. Here we have the origin of religious ceremonies. Eventually, the idea arose that the assistance of these spirits could be enlisted by means of prayer. At this stage, religion (magic), art and science were not differentiated. Lacking the means to gain real power over their environment, early humans attempted to obtain their ends by means of magical intercourse with nature, and thus subject it to their will.

zh: 早期人类对待他们的神灵和崇拜物的态度非常务实。祈祷的目的是为了获得结果。一个人会亲手制作一个偶像，并在其面前俯首膜拜。但如果期望的结果未能实现，他便会诅咒并殴打它，企图通过暴力手段夺取那些恳求未果之物。在这个充满梦境与鬼魂的奇异世界——这个宗教世界里，原始人的思维将每一件事都视为无形灵体所为。每一丛灌木、每一条溪流都是有生命的生物，或友善或敌对。每一个偶然事件、每一个梦境、每一阵疼痛或感觉，都是由某种灵体引起的。宗教解释填补了因缺乏对自然规律的了解而留下的空白。甚至死亡也不被视为自然现象，而是因冒犯了神灵而导致的后果。
en: The attitude of early humans to their spirit-gods and fetishes was quite practical. Prayers were intended to get results. A man would make an image with his own hands, and prostrate himself before it. But if the desired result was not forthcoming, he would curse it and beat it, in order to extract by violence what he failed to do by entreaty. In this strange world of dreams and ghosts, this world of religion, the primitive mind saw every happening as the work of unseen spirits. Every bush and stream was a living creature, friendly or hostile. Every chance event, every dream, pain or sensation, was caused by a spirit. Religious explanations filled the gap left by lack of knowledge of the laws of nature. Even death was not seen as a natural occurrence, but a result of some offence caused to the gods.

zh: 在人类漫长的历史长河中，绝大多数时间里，人们的头脑都充斥着此类观念。而且不仅存在于人们惯常视为“原始社会”的群体中。同类迷信观念至今仍以略有不同的形式存在。在文明那层薄薄的外衣之下，潜伏着原始的非理性倾向和观念，它们的根源可追溯至那个已被遗忘大半、却尚未被彻底克服的遥远过去。除非人类能够对自身的生存条件建立起牢固的掌控，否则这些观念也绝不会从人类意识中被彻底根除。
en: For the great majority of the existence of the human race, the minds of men and women have been full of this kind of thing. And not only in what people like to regard as primitive societies. The same kind of superstitious beliefs continue to exist, in slightly different guises, today. Beneath the thin veneer of civilisation, lurk primitive irrational tendencies and ideas which have their roots in a remote past which has been half-forgotten, but is not yet overcome. Nor will they be finally rooted out of human consciousness until men and women establish firm control over their conditions of existence.

zh: 劳动分工
en: DIVISION OF LABOUR

zh: 弗雷泽指出，早期人类社会中体力劳动与脑力劳动的分工，总是与祭司、萨满或巫师阶层的形成紧密相连：
en: Frazer points out that the division between manual and mental labour in early human society is invariably linked to the formation of a caste of priests, shamans or magicians:

zh: 众所周知，社会进步主要体现在职能的逐步分化上，或者用更通俗的话说，就是劳动分工。在原始社会中，原本人人都做、且完成得同样糟糕（或几乎如此）的工作，逐渐被分配给不同类别的劳动者，并被执行得越来越完美；只要这种专业化劳动所产生的物质或非物质产品能由全体成员共享，整个社区便能从日益加深的专业化中获益。如今，巫师或巫医似乎构成了社会演化过程中最古老的人为形成的阶层或职业阶层。因为在我们所知的每一个原始部落中都能找到巫师；而在最原始的部落中……他们是唯一存在的职业阶层。
en: Social progress, as we know, consists mainly in a successive differentiation of functions, or, in simpler language, a division of labour. The work which in primitive society is done by all alike and by all equally ill, or nearly so, is gradually distributed among different classes of workers and executed more and more perfectly; and so far as the products, material or immaterial, of his specialised labour are shared by all, the whole community benefits by the increasing specialisation. Now magicians or medicine-men appear to constitute the oldest artificial or professional class in the evolution of society. For sorcerers are found in every savage tribe known to us; and among the lowest savages… they are the only professional class that exists.

zh: 当然，弗雷泽所使用的语言并非我们今天所用的语言，但其基本思想仍然正确。将灵魂与身体、精神与物质、思考与行动割裂开来的二元论，在社会演化的某个特定阶段，因劳动分工的发展而获得了强有力的推动。脑力劳动与体力劳动的分离，是与社会阶级分化相伴生的现象。它标志着人类发展的一大进步。社会中的一小部分人首次摆脱了为获取生存必需品而劳动的必要性。拥有这种最珍贵的商品——闲暇，意味着人们可以将一生奉献给对星辰的研究。正如德国唯物主义哲学家路德维希·费尔巴哈所解释的，真正的理论科学始于宇宙学：
en: Of course, the language which Frazer uses is not the language we would use today, but the fundamental idea remains correct. The dualism which separates soul from body, mind from matter, thinking from doing, received a powerful impulse from the development of the division of labour at a given stage of social evolution. The separation between mental and manual labour is a phenomenon which coincides with the division of society into classes. It marked a great advance in human development. For the first time, a minority of society was freed from the necessity to work to obtain the essentials of existence. The possession of that most precious commodity, leisure, meant that men could devote their lives to the study of the stars. As the German materialist philosopher Ludwig Feuerbach explains, real theoretical science begins with cosmology:

zh: 动物只能感知那些直接影响其生命的光束；而人却能感知到最遥远恒星发出的、对其身体而言无关紧要的光线。唯有人拥有纯粹智性的、不涉利害的喜悦与激情；唯有人之眼才能举办理论的盛宴。那凝视星辰苍穹的眼睛，那注视着那既无用又无害、与地球及其生存需求毫无关联的光芒的眼睛——这双眼睛在那光芒中看到了自身的本质，其自身的起源。眼睛本质上是属天的。因此，人唯有通过眼睛才能将自己提升到超越尘世的高度；因此，理论始于对天体的观照。最早的哲学家都是天文学家。
en: The animal is sensible only of the beam which immediately affects life; while man perceives the ray, to him physically indifferent, of the remotest star. Man alone has purely intellectual, disinterested joys and passions; the eye of man alone keeps theoretic festivals. The eye which looks into the starry heavens, which gazes at that light, alike useless and harmless, having nothing in common with the earth and its necessities – this eye sees in that light its own nature, its own origin. The eye is heavenly in its nature. Hence man elevates himself above the earth only with the eye; hence theory begins with the contemplation of the heavens. The first philosophers were astronomers.

zh: 尽管在这一早期阶段，这仍与宗教以及祭司阶层的需求和利益交织在一起，但它同时也标志着人类文明的诞生。亚里士多德早已认识到这一点，他写道：
en: Although at this early stage this was still mixed up with religion and the requirements and interests of a priest caste, it also signified the birth of human civilisation. This was already understood by Aristotle, who wrote:

zh: 此外，这些理论学科是在人们拥有充裕闲暇时间的地方发展起来的：例如，数学起源于埃及，那里有一个神职阶层享有必要的闲暇。
en: These theoretical arts, moreover, were evolved in places where men had plenty of free time: mathematics, for example, originated in Egypt, where a priestly caste enjoyed the necessary leisure.

zh: 知识是权力的源泉。在任何艺术、科学和政权被少数人垄断的社会中，这一少数群体都会为了自身利益而运用并滥用其权力。尼罗河的年度泛滥对埃及人民而言是生死攸关的大事，因为他们的农作物完全依赖于此。埃及祭司们能够根据天文观测预测尼罗河何时会漫过河岸，这一能力必然极大地提升了他们在社会中的威望和权力。文字这一最强大的发明，是祭司阶层严加守护的秘密。正如普里戈金和斯滕格斯所评论的：
en: Knowledge is a source of power. In any society in which art, science and government is the monopoly of a few, that minority will use and abuse its power in its own interests. The annual flooding of the Nile was a matter of life and death to the people of Egypt, whose crops depended on it. The ability of the priests in Egypt to predict, on the basis of astronomical observations, when the Nile would flood its banks must have greatly increased their prestige and power over society. The art of writing, a most powerful invention, was the jealously guarded secret of the priest-caste. As Prigogine and Stengers comment:

zh: 苏美尔人发明了文字；苏美尔祭司推测，未来或许以某种隐秘的方式铭刻在当下我们周围发生的事件之中。他们甚至将这一信念系统化，将巫术与理性因素融合在一起。
en: Sumer discovered writing; the Sumerian priests speculated that the future might be written in some hidden way in the events taking place around us in the present. They even systematised this belief, mixing magical and rational elements.

zh: 劳动分工的进一步发展，在知识精英与被迫亲手劳动的人类大多数之间，造成了一道无法逾越的鸿沟。知识分子——无论是巴比伦祭司还是现代理论物理学家——只知一种劳动，即脑力劳动。在数千年的历程中，脑力劳动相对于“粗鄙”的体力劳动的优越性已深深植根于人心，并演变为一种偏见。语言、词语和思想被赋予了近乎神秘的力量。文化成为特权精英的垄断品，他们严密地守护着自己的秘密，并为了自身利益而利用和滥用其地位。
en: The further development of the division of labour gave rise to an unbridgeable gulf between the intellectual elite and the majority of humankind, condemned to labour with their hands. The intellectual, whether Babylonian priest or modern theoretical physicist, knows only one kind of labour, mental labour. Over the course of millennia, the superiority of the latter over ‘crude’ manual labour becomes deeply ingrained and acquires the force of a prejudice. Language, words and thoughts become endowed with almost mystical powers. Culture becomes the monopoly of a privileged elite, which jealously guards its secrets, and uses and abuses its position in its own interests.

zh: 在古代，知识分子贵族从不掩饰其对体力劳动的蔑视。以下摘自一部约公元前2000 年撰写的埃及文本《职业讽刺诗》，据称是一位父亲对儿子的告诫——他正将儿子送往书写学校接受书吏的培训：
en: In ancient times, the intellectual aristocracy made no attempt to conceal its contempt for physical labour. The following extract from an Egyptian text known as The Satire on the Trades, written about 2000 BC, is supposed to consist of a father’s exhortation to his son, whom he is sending to the Writing School to train as a scribe:

zh: 我曾目睹劳苦之人如何受苦——你应当全心致力于书写之道。我也曾观察到人如何能从职责中解脱出来［原文如此！］——看啊，没有什么能胜过书写……
我曾目睹金属匠在熔炉前劳作。他的手指宛如鳄鱼；他散发的臭味比鱼子还要难闻……
小建筑承包商搬运泥土……他踩在泥里，比葡萄藤或猪还要脏。他的衣服被泥土弄得僵硬……
制箭匠，当他走进沙漠［去采集燧石箭头］时，显得十分凄惨。他给驴子的那份报酬，远比驴子此后所做的活计［所值］的还要多……
洗衣工在［河］岸边洗衣服，与鳄鱼为邻……
看哪，没有哪种职业能免于受老板管束——唯有书吏：他自己就是老板……
看哪，没有哪位书吏会缺乏来自王室财产的食粮——生命、繁荣、健康！……他的父母赞美神，因他已被引上生者的道路。看哪，这些事——我［已将它们摆］在你和你子孙的子孙面前。
en: I have seen how the belaboured man is belaboured – thou shouldst set thy heart in pursuit of writing. And I have observed how one may be rescued from his duties [sic!] – behold, there is nothing which surpasses writing…
I have seen the metalworker at his work at the mouth of his furnace. His fingers were somewhat like crocodiles; he stank more than fish-roe…
The small building contractor carries mud … He is dirtier than vines or pigs from treading under his mud. His clothes are stiff with clay…
The arrow-maker, he is very miserable as he goes out into the desert [to get flint points]. Greater is that which he gives to his donkey than its work thereafter [is worth]…
The laundry man launders on the [river] bank, a neighbour of the crocodile…
Behold, there is no profession free of a boss – except for the scribe: he is the boss…

Behold, there is no scribe who lacks food from the property of the House of the King – life, prosperity, health! … His father and his mother praise god, he being set upon the way of the living. Behold these things – I [have set them] before thee and thy children’s children.
body.review: 原文将泥工与 vines or pigs 相比，其中 vines（葡萄藤）照录；[sic!]及其他方括号来自英文底本。

zh: 这种态度在希腊人中也很普遍，正如雅典的色诺芬在这段文字中所显示的：
en: The same attitude was prevalent among the Greeks, as can be seen in this passage from Xenophon of Athens:

zh: 所谓“手工技艺”，在我们的城邦中背负着社会污名，理应受到鄙视，因为这些技艺损害了从业者或监工的身体——迫使他们过着久坐不动、闭门不出的生活，有时甚至整日守在炉火旁。这种身体的退化也会导致灵魂的堕落。此外，从事这些行业的工人根本没有时间履行友谊或公民义务。因此，他们被视为不称职的朋友和不称职的爱国者；在某些城邦——尤其是好战的城邦——公民从事手工业是违法的。
en: What are called the mechanical arts, carry a social stigma and are rightly dishonoured in our cities, for these arts damage the bodies of those who work in them or who act as overseers, by compelling them to a sedentary life and to an indoor life, and, in some cases, to spend the whole day by the fire. This physical degeneration results also in deterioration of the soul. Furthermore, the workers at these trades simply have not got the time to perform the offices of friendship or citizenship. Consequently they are looked upon as bad friends and bad patriots, and in some cities, especially the warlike ones, it is not legal for a citizen to ply a mechanical trade.

zh: 脑力劳动与体力劳动之间的彻底割裂，加深了这样一种错觉：即观念、思想和言语具有独立的存在。这种误解是所有宗教和哲学唯心主义的核心。
en: The radical divorce between mental and manual labour deepens the illusion that ideas, thoughts and words have an independent existence. This misconception lies at the heart of all religion and philosophical idealism.

zh: 并非上帝按照自己的形象创造了人，恰恰相反，是人们按照自己的形象和模样创造了诸神。路德维希·费尔巴哈曾说，如果鸟类有宗教，它们的神就会长着翅膀。
en: It was not God who created man after his own image, but, on the contrary, men and women who created gods in their own image and likeness. Ludwig Feuerbach said that if birds had a religion, their God would have wings.

zh: 宗教是一种梦境，在其中，我们自身的观念和情感似乎成了独立的存在，成了我们自身之外的实体。宗教心态不区分主观与客观——它毫无怀疑；它所具备的能力，并非辨别自身以外的事物，而是将自身的观念视为自身之外的、独立的实体。
en: Religion is a dream, in which our own conceptions and emotions appear to us as separate existences, beings out of ourselves. The religious mind does not distinguish between subjective and objective – it has no doubts; it has the faculty, not of discerning other things than itself, but of seeing its own conceptions out of itself as distinct beings.

zh: 科洛丰的克塞诺芬尼等先贤早已洞悉这一点，他写道：
en: This was already understood by men like Xenophanes of Colophon, who wrote:

zh: 荷马和赫西俄德将人类之间一切可耻且不光彩的行为都赋予了诸神：偷窃、通奸以及相互欺骗……埃塞俄比亚人将他们的神描绘成黑皮肤、扁鼻子的形象，而色雷斯人则将他们的神描绘成灰眼睛、红头发的形象……如果动物也能像人类一样绘画和制作物品，那么马和牛也会按照它们自己的形象来塑造诸神。
en: Homer and Hesiod have ascribed to the gods every deed that is shameful and dishonourable among men: stealing and adultery and deceiving each other … The Ethiopians make their gods black and snub-nosed, and the Thracians theirs grey-eyed and red-haired … If animals could paint and make things, like men, horses and oxen too would fashion the gods in their own image.

zh: 几乎所有宗教中都存在的创世神话，其意象无一例外地取材于现实生活，例如，陶工将尚未成形的泥土塑造成型的形象。戈登·柴尔德认为，《创世记》第一卷中的创世故事反映了这样一个事实：在美索不达米亚，“起初”大地确实与水分开了，但这并非由神明干预所致：
en: The Creation myths which exist in almost all religions invariably take their images from real life, for example, the image of the potter who gives form to formless clay. In the opinion of Gordon Childe, the story of the Creation in the first book of Genesis reflects the fact that, in Mesopotamia the land was indeed separated from the waters “in the Beginning”, but not by divine intervention:
body.review: 英文底本写作“the first book of Genesis”，译文保留其“《创世记》第一卷”的表述。

zh: 巴比伦那些伟大城市将要崛起的土地，从字面上说必须被创造出来；《圣经》中埃雷克城的史前前身，便建在一种由芦苇交错铺在冲积泥土上形成的平台上。希伯来《创世记》让我们熟悉了关于苏美尔原始状态的更古老传统——那是一种“混沌”状态，其中水与陆地的界限仍未定型。创世中的一个关键事件便是将这些元素分隔开来。然而，创造这片土地的并非神明，而是原始苏美尔人自己；他们开凿渠道以灌溉田地、排干沼泽；他们修建堤坝和堆砌平台，以保护人和牲畜免受洪水侵袭，并将他们抬升至洪水之上；他们在芦苇丛中开辟了第一片空地，并探索了芦苇丛之间的水道。传统中对这场奋斗的记忆之所以如此顽强地延续下来，在某种程度上反映了古代苏美尔人所承受的艰辛。他们的回报是源源不断的营养丰富的椰枣、从他们排干的田地里收获的丰硕庄稼，以及供羊群和牛群永久放牧的牧场。
en: The land on which the great cities of Babylonia were to rise had literally to be created; the prehistoric forerunner of the biblical Erech was built on a sort of platform of reeds, laid criss-cross upon the alluvial mud. The Hebrew book of Genesis has familiarised us with much older traditions of the pristine condition of Sumer – a ‘chaos’ in which the boundaries between water and dry land were still fluid. An essential incident in ‘The Creation’ is the separation of these elements. Yet it was no god, but the proto-Sumerian themselves who created the land; they dug channels to water the fields and drain the marsh; they built dykes and mounded platforms to protect men and cattle from the waters and raise them above the flood; they made the first clearings in the reed brakes and explored the channels between them. The tenacity with which the memory of this struggle persisted in tradition is some measure of the exertion imposed upon the ancient Sumerians. Their reward was an assured supply of nourishing dates, a bounteous harvest from the fields they had drained, and permanent pastures for flocks and herds.

zh: 人类最早试图解释世界及其在世界中的位置时，这些尝试往往与神话交织在一起。巴比伦人相信，神马尔杜克“从混沌中创造了秩序”，将陆地与水、天与地分隔开来。《圣经》中的创世神话是由犹太人从巴比伦人那里借鉴而来，后来又融入了基督教文化。科学思想的真正历史始于人类学会摒弃神话，并试图在不依赖神明干预的情况下，对自然进行理性理解之时。从那一刻起，人类为摆脱物质和精神枷锁而进行的真正斗争便拉开了序幕。
en: Man’s earliest attempts to explain the world and his place in it were mixed up with mythology. The Babylonians believed that the god Marduk created ‘Order out of Chaos’, separating the land from the water, heaven from earth. The biblical Creation myth was taken from the Babylonians by the Jews, and later passed into the culture of Christianity. The true history of scientific thought commences when men and women learn to dispense with mythology, and attempt to obtain a rational understanding of nature, without the intervention of the gods. From that moment, the real struggle for the emancipation of humanity from material and spiritual bondage begins.

zh: 思想的革命
en: A REVOLUTION IN THOUGHT

zh: 哲学的出现标志着人类思想中一场真正的革命。正如现代文明的许多方面一样，我们要归功于古希腊人。尽管印度人、中国人以及后来的阿拉伯人也取得了重要进展，但在文艺复兴之前，正是希腊人将哲学和科学发展到了巅峰。从公元前七世纪中叶起长达四百年的希腊思想史，构成了人类历史长河中最壮丽的篇章之一。
en: The advent of philosophy represents a genuine revolution in human thought. Like so much of modern civilisation, we owe it to the ancient Greeks. Although important advances were also made by the Indians and Chinese, and later the Arabs, it was the Greeks who developed philosophy and science to its highest point prior to the Renaissance. The history of Greek thought in the four hundred year period, from the middle of the seventh century BC, constitutes one of the most imposing pages in the annals of human history.

zh: 这里有一长串开拓思想发展道路的英雄人物。早在哥伦布之前，希腊人就发现世界是圆的；早在达尔文之前，他们就解释了人类是从鱼类进化而来的；他们在数学领域，尤其是几何学方面，取得了非凡的发现，此后一千五百年间，人们在这些发现的基础上都未能取得多大进展；他们发明了力学，甚至发明了蒸汽机。
en: Here we have a long line of heroes who pioneered the development of thought. The Greeks discovered that the world was round long before Columbus. They explained that humans had evolved from fishes long before Darwin. They made extraordinary discoveries in mathematics, especially geometry, which were not greatly improved upon for one-and-a-half millennia. They invented mechanics and even invented the steam engine.

zh: 这种观察世界的方式之所以令人惊叹，在于它并非基于宗教。与埃及人和巴比伦人截然不同——尽管他们从后者那里学到了很多——希腊思想家并不借助神灵来解释自然现象。人类首次试图纯粹从自然的角度来阐释自然的运作规律。这是整个人类思想史上最重大的转折点之一。真正的科学由此开始。
en: What was startlingly new about this way of looking at the world was that it was not religious. In complete contrast to the Egyptians and Babylonians, from whom they had learnt a lot, the Greek thinkers did not resort to gods and goddesses to explain natural phenomena. For the first time, men and women sought to explain the workings of nature purely in terms of nature. This was one of the greatest turning points in the entire history of human thought. True science starts here.

zh: 哲学的诞生
en: THE BIRTH OF PHILOSOPHY

zh: 西方哲学诞生于早期爱琴海时代那片晴朗湛蓝的天空之下。公元前八世纪至七世纪，地中海东部正经历着经济快速扩张的时期。那是一个令人振奋的时代。位于今土耳其海岸外的爱奥尼亚群岛上的希腊人，与埃及、巴比伦和吕底亚开展了繁荣的贸易。约公元前625 年，吕底亚人发明的货币经由埃伊纳岛传入欧洲，极大地刺激了贸易，随之而来的是，有些人获得了巨大财富，而另一些人却陷入了债务和奴役。
en: Western philosophy was born under the clear blue skies of the early Aegean period. The eighth and seventh centuries BC were a period of rapid economic expansion in the eastern Mediterranean. These were stirring times. The Greeks of the Ionian islands, which lie off the coast of present-day Turkey, conducted a thriving trade with Egypt, Babylon and Lydia. The Lydian invention of money was introduced into Europe via Aegina at about 625 BC, greatly stimulating trade, bringing in its wake great riches for some and indebtedness and slavery for others.

zh: 最早的希腊哲学标志着哲学真正的起点。这是人类试图挣脱迷信与神话的古老桎梏，摒弃众神与女神，从而首次能够直面自然以及真实的男女。
en: The earliest Greek philosophy represents the true starting point of philosophy. It is an attempt to struggle free from the age-old bounds of superstition and myth, to dispense with gods and goddesses, so that, for the first time, human beings could stand face to face with nature and with real men and women.

zh: 经济革命催生了新的社会矛盾。旧的父权制社会的瓦解引发了贫富之间的冲突。旧贵族阶层面临着民众的不满以及“僭主”们的反对——这些“僭主”往往正是持异议的贵族本人，他们总是乐于站在民众起义的前列。一个动荡不安的时期由此开启，人们开始对旧有的信仰提出质疑。
en: The economic revolution gave rise to new social contradictions. The breakdown of the old patriarchal society provoked a clash between rich and poor. The old aristocracy was faced with the discontent of the masses and the opposition of the ‘tyrants’ – frequently dissident nobles themselves – who were always willing to put themselves at the head of popular risings. A period of instability opened up, in which men and women began to question the old beliefs.

zh: 以下段落描述了当时雅典的状况：
en: The situation in Athens at this time is described in the following passage:

zh: 在歉收之年，他们［农民］不得不向富有的邻居借粮；但随着货币的出现，这意味着：人们不再像过去那样以邻里互助的方式借一袋谷物，而是必须在收成前谷物价格低廉时，借够维持生计所需的谷物金额；或者，支付高额利息——正是这种利息曾在梅加拉引发了如此强烈的愤慨。到公元前600 年，富人将货物出口到埃伊纳岛或科林斯等畅销市场，而穷人却在挨饿。许多人还因土地被拿作债务抵押而失去土地，甚至失去自由；因为债权人对无力偿还债务的债务人所能采取的最后手段，就是将他及其家人作为奴隶扣押。这条法律很严苛；它是富人的法律。
en: In the bad years they [the peasants] had to borrow from rich neighbours; but with the coming of money, this meant that, instead of borrowing a sack of corn in the good old neighbourly way, one had to borrow the price of enough corn to tide one over, before the harvest, when it was cheap; or alternatively, to pay heavy interest, of the kind that raised such indignation at Megara. By 600 [BC], while rich men exported to good markets in Aegina or Corinth, poor men were going hungry. Many, too, were losing their land, pledged as security for debts, and even their liberty; for the debtor’s last recourse against the insolvent debtor was to seize him and his family as slaves. The law was harsh; it was rich man’s law.
body.review: 英文底本写作“the debtor’s last recourse against the insolvent debtor”，前一个debtor疑为creditor之误。此处按语境及已有译稿译为“债权人”，英文照录，特此说明。

zh: 这些法律由德拉科编纂成法典，由此衍生出的“德拉科式法律”一词已成为严刑峻法的代称。
en: These laws were put into a code by Drakon, from which the phrase ‘Draconian laws’ has become proverbial.

zh: 动荡的公元前六世纪是小亚细亚希腊爱奥尼亚共和国衰落时期，其特征是社会危机以及富人与穷人、主人与奴隶之间激烈的阶级斗争。罗斯托夫采夫写道：“在米利都［小亚细亚］，民众起初获胜，并杀害了贵族们的妻儿；随后贵族们占据上风，将对手活活烧死，用活人火炬照亮了城市的空地。”
en: The turbulent sixth century BC was a period of decline of the Greek Ionian republics of Asia Minor, characterised by social crisis and ferocious class struggle between rich and poor, masters and slaves. Rostovtsev writes: “At Miletus [in Asia Minor] the people were at first victorious and murdered the wives and children of the aristocrats; then the aristocrats prevailed and burned their opponents alive, lighting up the open spaces of the city with live torches”.

zh: 当时小亚细亚其他大多数希腊城邦的情况也与此类似。这个时代的英雄与后来那种将哲学家视为与世隔绝、蜗居象牙塔中的形象毫无共同之处。这些“智者”不仅是思想家，更是行动者；不仅是理论家，更是通晓世事的实干家。关于其中首位——米利都的泰勒斯（约公元前640—546 年）——我们几乎一无所知，但有明确记载表明，他直到晚年才投身哲学。他还涉足商业、工程学、几何学和天文学（据说他曾预言过一次日食，该日食应发生于公元前585 年）。
en: These conditions were typical of most other Greek cities of Asia Minor at the time. The heroes of this age had nothing in common with the later idea of the philosopher, isolated from the rest of humanity in his ivory tower. These ‘wise men’ were not only thinkers, but doers, not only theoreticians, but practical men of the world. Of the first of them, Thales of Miletus (c. 640-546 BC), we know next to nothing, but it is expressly stated that it was only late in life that he took to philosophy. He was also involved in commerce, engineering, geometry and astronomy (he is said to have predicted an eclipse, which must have occurred in 585 BC).

zh: 无可争议的是，所有早期希腊哲学家都是唯物主义者。他们背离神话，试图通过观察自然本身来寻找自然运作的一般规律。后世的希腊人称他们为“物活论者”，可译为“认为物质具有生命的人”。这种将物质视为具有自发运动能力的观念，其现代性令人惊叹，且远胜于十八世纪的机械物理学。鉴于缺乏现代科学仪器，他们的理论往往带有灵感臆测的性质。但考虑到资源匮乏，令人惊叹的是，他们竟如此接近对自然运行规律的真正理解。因此，哲学家阿那克西曼德（约公元前610—545 年）推断出，人类和所有其他动物都是由一种鱼类演化而来的，这种鱼类离开了水，登上了陆地。
en: What is indisputable is that all the early Greek philosophers were materialists. Turning their backs on mythology, they sought to find a general principle for the workings of nature from an observation of nature itself. The later Greeks refer to them as hylozoists, which can be translated as “those who think that matter is alive”. This conception of matter as self-moving is strikingly modern, and far superior to the mechanical physics of the eighteenth century. Given the absence of modern scientific instruments, their theories frequently had the character of inspired guesswork. But, taking into account the lack of resources, the amazing thing is how close they came to a real understanding of the workings of nature. Thus the philosopher Anaximander (c. 610-545 BC) worked out that man and all other animals had developed from a fish, which abandoned water for the land.

zh: 仅因这些哲学家在论及第一实体时使用了“神”（theos）一词，就认为他们信奉宗教，这种看法是具有误导性的。J. 伯内特指出，这只不过相当于荷马诗中“不衰老的”、“不朽的”等古老的修饰语。即使在荷马的作品中，该词也被赋予了多种不同的含义。从赫西俄德的《神谱》中可以清楚地看出，许多“神”从未被崇拜过，而仅仅是自然现象甚至人类情感的便利拟人化。原始宗教将天空视为神圣的，并与大地区分开来。爱奥尼亚哲学家们彻底打破了这一观点。虽然他们以巴比伦和埃及宇宙学的诸多发现为基础，但他们摒弃了将天文学与占星术混为一谈的神话元素。
en: It is misleading to suppose that these philosophers were religious just because they used the word ‘god’ (theos) in relation to primary substance. J. Burnet states that this meant no more than the old Homeric epithets like ‘ageless’, ‘deathless’, etc. Even in Homer, the word is used in several different senses. From Hesiod’s Theogony it is clear that many of the ‘gods’ were never worshipped, but were merely convenient personifications of natural phenomena or even human passions. Primitive religions looked on the heavens as divine and set apart from the earth. The Ionian philosophers radically broke with this standpoint. While basing themselves on the many discoveries of Babylonian and Egyptian cosmology, they rejected the mythical element, which confused astronomy with astrology.

zh: 苏格拉底之前的希腊哲学总体倾向于探索自然的根本原理：
en: The general tendency of Greek philosophy before Socrates was to search for the underlying principles of nature:

zh: 正是自然——那最直接呈现在我们面前、最贴近视线、最可感知的存在——首先唤起了探究精神。人们认为，在其千变万化的形态和纷繁复杂的现象之下，必定存在着一个最初且恒久不变的基本原理。这个原理是什么？人们问道：万物的原始根基是什么？或者更确切地说，哪种自然元素是基础元素？
en: Nature it was – that which is most immediately present to us, that which lies nearest the eye, that which is palpablest – that first attracted the spirit of inquiry. Under its changeful forms, its multiplex phenomena, there must lie, it was thought, a first and permanent fundamental principle. What is this principle? What, it was asked, is the primitive ground of things? Or, more precisely, what natural element is the basal element?

zh: 对此，他们给出了不同的解释。例如，泰勒斯主张万物的基础是水。这对人类思想而言是一次巨大的进步。诚然，早在很久以前，巴比伦人在他们的创世神话中就提出了“万物源于水”的观点，而《创世记》第一卷中的希伯来创世故事正是以此为蓝本。传说中说：“所有陆地原本都是大海”，直到巴比伦的创世神马尔杜克将陆地与大海分开。这里的区别在于，这里没有马尔杜克，也没有站在自然之外的神圣创世者。相反，自然首次被用纯粹的唯物主义观点来解释，即从自然本身的角度来解释。
en: They gave different explanations for this. For example, Thales claimed that the basis of all things is water. This was a great advance for human thought. True, the Babylonians had long before put forward the idea that all things came from water in their Creation myth, which was the model for the Hebrew story of the Creation in the first book of Genesis. “All lands were sea”, says the legend, until Marduk, the Babylonian creator, separated the land from the sea. The difference here is that there is no Marduk, no divine creator standing outside nature. Instead, for the first time, nature is explained in purely materialist terms, that is, in terms of nature itself.

zh: 将自然归结为水的观点，其实并没有表面上看起来那么牵强。撇开地球表面绝大多数由水构成这一事实不谈——这一点爱奥尼亚希腊人尤为清楚——水对所有生命形式都至关重要。我们身体的大部分由水构成，一旦缺水，我们将很快死亡。此外，水会改变形态，从液体转变为固体，再转变为蒸汽。对此，伯内特评论道：
en: Nor is the idea of nature as reducible to water as far-fetched as it might appear. Apart from the fact that the great majority of the earth’s surface is made up of water, something the Ionian Greeks above all were aware of, water is essential for all forms of life. The bulk of our body consists of water, and we would quickly die if deprived of it. Moreover, water changes its form, passing from a liquid to a solid, to a vapour. On this Burnet comments:

zh: 不难看出，气象方面的考量可能促使泰勒斯采纳了他的观点。在我们所知的一切事物中，水似乎能呈现出最多样的形态。我们熟悉它的固体、液体和气态形式，因此，泰勒斯很可能认为，他亲眼目睹了世界从水产生、又回归水的过程。蒸发现象自然让人联想到，天体的“火”是由它们从海中汲取的水分维持的。即使在今天，人们仍会说“太阳把水吸上去”。水又以雨的形式降落；最后，正如早期宇宙学家所认为的那样，它化作了泥土。对于那些熟悉埃及河流——正是这些河流形成了三角洲——以及小亚细亚的湍急河流冲积下大量沉积物的人来说，这或许显得足够自然。
en: Nor is it hard to see how the meteorological considerations may have led Thales to adopt the views he did. Of all the things we know, water seems to take the most various shapes. It is familiar to us in a solid, a liquid, and a vaporous form, and so, Thales may well have thought he saw the world-process from water and back to water again going on before his eyes. The phenomenon of evaporation naturally suggests that the fire of the heavenly bodies is kept up by the moisture they draw from the sea. Even at the present day, people speak of the ‘sun drawing up water’. Water comes down again in rain; and lastly, so the early cosmologists thought, it turns to earth. This may have seemed natural enough to men who were familiar with the rivers of Egypt which had formed the Delta, and the torrents of Asia Minor which bring down large alluvial deposits.

zh: 阿那克西曼德
en: ANAXIMANDER

zh: 泰勒斯之后，其他哲学家提出了关于物质基本结构的不同理论。据说阿那克西曼德来自萨摩斯岛，著名的毕达哥拉斯也曾居住于此。据称他撰写过关于自然、恒星、地球球体及其他问题的著作。他绘制了一幅类似地图的图示，标明了陆地与海洋的边界，并发明了多项数学工具，包括日晷和天文图。
en: Thales was followed by other philosophers who advanced different theories as to the basic structure of matter. Anaximander is said to have come from Samos, where the famous Pythagoras also lived. He is said to have written about nature, the fixed stars, the earth’s sphere and other matters. He produced something like a map, showing the boundary of land and sea, and was responsible for a number of mathematical inventions, including a sundial and an astronomical chart.
body.review: “来自萨摩斯岛”为本书原文的表述，译文照录。

zh: 与泰勒斯一样，阿那克西曼德也思考过现实的本质是什么。他同样从严格的唯物主义角度来探讨这个问题，不诉诸神灵或任何超自然因素。但与同时代的泰勒斯不同，他并未试图从某种特定的物质形式（如水）中寻找答案。据第欧根尼记载：
en: Like Thales, Anaximander considered what the nature of reality was. Like him, he approached this question from a strictly materialist point of view, without recourse to the gods or any supernatural elements. But, unlike his contemporary, Thales, he did not seek to find the answer in a particular form of matter, such as water. According to Diogenes:

zh: 他将“无限”（即未被确定的）作为本源和元素；他既未将其界定为空气，也未将其界定为水，或任何类似的事物。……它是万物生成与消亡的根本；在漫长的间隔中，无穷的世界或神明由此诞生，又重新消逝于其中。
en: He adduced the Infinite (the undetermined) as principle and element; he neither determined it as air or water or any such thing. … It is the principle of all becoming and passing away; at long intervals infinite worlds or gods rise out of it, and again they pass away into the same.

zh: 这首次将宇宙研究置于科学基础之上，并使早期希腊哲学家得以做出远超其时代的杰出发现。他们首先发现世界是圆的，并不依附于任何事物；地球并非宇宙的中心，而是与其他行星一同围绕着中心旋转。据另一位同时代人希波利托斯所述，阿那克西曼德认为地球自由悬浮，不受任何事物束缚，因为它与万物等距，且形状呈圆形、内部中空，如同柱子一般，因此我们位于地球的一侧，而其他人则在另一侧。他们还发现了日食和月食的真实理论。
en: This put the study of the universe on a scientific footing for the first time, and enabled the early Greek philosophers to make outstanding discoveries, far in advance of their time. They first discovered that the world is round and does not rest on anything, that the earth was not the centre of the universe, but revolves with the other planets around the centre. According to another contemporary, Hippolitos, Anaximander said that the earth swings free, held in place by nothing, because it is equidistant from everything, and is round in shape and hollow, like a pillar, so that we are on one side of the earth, and others on the other. They also discovered the true theory of lunar and solar eclipses.
body.review: 原文称希波利托斯为“另一位同时代人”，并作出本段天文学归属判断；这些均按底本保留。swings free译为自由悬浮，不据旧译增添旋转之意。

zh: 尽管存在种种漏洞和不足，这些思想仍展现出对自然与宇宙惊人地大胆而独创的构想，无疑比中世纪那种目光短浅的神秘主义更接近真理——那时人类的思想再次被宗教教条所束缚。此外，这些重要的进步并非仅仅源于猜测，而是经过深思熟虑、调查研究和实验得出的结果。在达尔文之前2000 年，阿那克西曼德就凭借其在海洋生物学方面的惊人发现，预见了进化论。历史学家A. R. 伯恩认为，这绝非偶然，而是科学探究的结果：“看起来他似乎曾对胚胎和化石进行过观察——正如他的某位继任者确实做过的那样；但我们没有得到明确的记载。”
en: With all their gaps and deficiencies, these ideas represent a startlingly bold and original conception of nature and the universe, certainly far nearer to the truth than the blinkered mysticism of the Middle Ages, when human thought was again shackled by religious dogma. Moreover, these important advances were not merely the result of guesswork, but the result of careful thought, investigation and experiment. 2000 years before Darwin, Anaximander anticipated the theory of evolution, with his amazing discoveries in marine biology. The historian A. R. Burn believes that this was no accident, but the result of scientific investigation: “It looks as though he had made observations on embryos and also on fossils, as one of his successors certainly did; but we are not positively told.”

zh: 阿那克西曼德在人类思想史上引发了一场伟大的革命。他不再局限于某种具体的物质形态，而是提出了“物质”这一普遍概念——即作为哲学概念的物质。这种普遍的物质是永恒的、无限的，处于不断变化与演化的过程中。我们通过感官所感知到的万千存在形式，都是同一基本实体的不同表现。这一思想如此新颖，以至于许多人难以理解。普鲁塔克曾抱怨说，阿那克西曼德没有明确指出他的“无限”究竟是哪一种元素——水、土、气还是火。但正是在这一点上，该理论才具有划时代的意义。
en: Anaximander effected a great revolution in human thought. Instead of limiting himself to this or that concrete form of matter, he arrived at the concept of matter in general, matter as a philosophical concept. This universal substance is eternal and infinite, constantly changing and evolving. All the myriad forms of being we perceive through our senses are different expressions of the same basic substance. This idea was so novel that for many it proved incomprehensible. Plutarch complained that Anaximander did not specify which one of the elements his Infinite was – water, earth, air or fire. But precisely in this lay the epoch-making character of the theory.

zh: 阿那克西美尼
en: ANAXIMENES

zh: 爱奥尼亚唯物主义“三大巨头”中的最后一位是阿那克西美尼（约公元前585—528 年）。据说他出生于泰勒斯“鼎盛”之时，而他自己的“鼎盛”之时恰逢泰勒斯去世。他比阿那克西曼德年轻。与阿那克西曼德不同，他追随泰勒斯，将单一元素——空气——视为绝对实体，万物由此产生，最终亦归于此。事实上，阿那克西美尼对“空气”（aer）一词的用法与现代用法有实质区别。它包括蒸汽、雾气，甚至黑暗。许多译者更倾向于使用“雾”一词。
en: The last of the great trio of Ionian materialists was Anaximenes (c. 585-528 BC). He is said to have been born when Thales ‘flourished’, and to have ‘flourished’ when Thales died. He was younger than Anaximander. Unlike Anaximander, and following Thales, he took a single element – air – as the absolute substance, from which everything comes forth and to which everything is ultimately reduced. In fact, Anaximenes’ use of the word ‘air’ (aer) differs substantially from the modern usage. It includes vapour, mist and even darkness. Many translators prefer the word ‘mist’.

zh: 乍看之下，这一思想似乎较之阿那克西曼德所提出的关于物质的一般性观点有所倒退。但实际上，他的世界观却是向前迈进了一步。
en: At first sight, this idea represents a step back in comparison to the position of matter in general arrived at by Anaximander. In fact, his world view was a step forward.

zh: 阿那克西美尼试图阐明，作为普遍实体的“空气”如何通过他所称的“稀化”与“凝聚”过程发生转化。当它稀化时，便成为火；当它凝聚时，便成为风。通过进一步的凝聚，我们便得到了云、水、土和石头。然而，尽管就细节而言，他的宇宙观与阿那克西曼德的相比略显逊色（例如，他认为世界呈桌子状），但他的哲学仍代表了一种进步，因为他试图超越对物质本质的笼统陈述。他试图通过稀化与凝聚的过程，不仅在质上，而且在量上，对物质进行更精确的界定。用法林顿教授的话说：
en: Anaximenes attempted to show how ‘air’, the universal substance, becomes transformed through a process of what he called rarification and condensation. When it is rarefied, it becomes fire, when condensed, wind. By further condensation, we get clouds, water, earth and stones. But, although in details his view of the universe compares unfavourably with that of Anaximander (he thought the world was shaped like a table, for instance), nevertheless, his philosophy represented an advance, inasmuch as he tried to move beyond a general statement of the nature of matter. He attempted to give it a more precise determination, not only qualitatively, but quantitatively, through the process of rarification and condensation. In the words of Professor Farrington:

zh: 在追溯这一系列思想家的历程时，请注意观察：随着他们不断钻研问题，其逻辑思维、思想储备和抽象能力是如何不断提升的。当泰勒斯将万物的多种表象归结为一个“第一本原”时，人类思维取得了重大进步。当阿那克西曼德选择的“第一本原”不是像水那样可见的事物形态，而是一个像“不定者”这样的概念时，又迈出了重要一步。但阿那克西美尼仍不满足。当阿那克西曼德试图解释不同事物如何从“不定者”中产生时，他给出的答案仅仅是一个比喻。他说这是一个“分离”的过程。阿那克西美尼认为还需要更多内容，于是提出了“稀化”和“凝聚”这两个互补的概念，从而解释了量变如何产生质变。
en: Observe, in following this succession of thinkers, how their logic, their stock of ideas, their power of abstraction, increase as they grapple with their problem. It was a great advance in human thinking when Thales reduced the manifold appearances of things to one First Principle. Another great step was taken when Anaximander chose, as his First Principle, not a visible form of things like water, but a concept like the Indeterminate. But Anaximenes was still not content. When Anaximander sought to explain how the different things emerged from the Indeterminate, he gave a reply that was a mere metaphor. He said it was a process of ‘separating out’. Anaximenes felt that something more was needed, and came forward with the complementary ideas of Rarification and Condensation, which offered an explanation of how quantitative changes could produce qualitative ones.

zh: 鉴于当时的技术水平，阿那克西美尼无法对所探讨的现象给出更精确的描述。人们很容易指出其观点中的缺陷甚至荒谬之处，但这恰恰偏离了重点。不能责怪早期希腊哲学家未能为其世界图景提供详细的内容，因为这只有在随后2000 多年的经济、技术和科学进步的基础上才成为可能。这些人类思想的伟大先驱为人类做了一件无与伦比的贡献：他们摆脱了宗教迷信的陈旧习俗，从而奠定了基础——没有这一基础，一切科学和文化进步都是不可想象的。
en: Given the existing level of technique, it was impossible for Anaximenes to arrive at a more precise characterisation of the phenomena under consideration. It is easy to point to the deficiencies and even absurdities of his views. But this would miss the point. The early Greek philosophers cannot be blamed for failing to provide their world picture with a detailed content, which was only possible on the basis of over 2000 years of subsequent economic, technological and scientific advance. These great pioneers of human thought rendered humanity the unique service of breaking away from the age-old habits of religious superstition, and thereby laid the foundation without which all scientific and cultural advance would have been unthinkable.

zh: 此外，这些伟大的革命性思想家所阐述的关于宇宙和自然的总体观点，在许多方面都接近真理。他们的问题在于，鉴于当时生产力和技术的发展水平，他们缺乏验证假设并使其建立在坚实基础上的手段。他们预见了许多只有现代科学——以远更高水平的科学技术发展为基础——才能充分阐明的东西。因此，对于阿那克西美尼而言，“空气”仅仅是物质在其最简单、最基本形式下的简写。正如现代物理学的奠基人之一埃尔温·薛定谔机智地指出的那样：“倘若他当时说的是‘解离的氢气’” （虽然很难指望他会这么说），“他的观点就不会与我们当今的观点相去甚远”。
en: Moreover, the general view of the universe and nature elaborated by these great revolutionary thinkers was in many respects close to the truth. Their problem was that, given the level of development of production and technology, they did not have the means of testing their hypotheses, and putting them on a solid footing. They anticipated many things which could only be fully worked out by modern science, resting on a far higher development of science and technique. Thus, for Anaximenes, ‘air’ is only shorthand for matter in its simplest, most basic form. As Erwin Schrödinger, one of the founders of modern physics shrewdly remarked: “Had he said dissociated hydrogen gas”, (which he could hardly be expected to say), “he would not be so far from our present view”.

zh: 早期的爱奥尼亚自然哲学家们，可能已经尽其所能地通过思辨理性来解释自然的运作机制。这些确实是伟大的概括，指明了正确的方向。但为了将这一进程推进得更远，有必要更详细地考察事物，逐步对自然进行逐一分析。这一工作后来由亚里士多德和亚历山大里亚的希腊思想家们开创。而这项任务的一个重要部分，是从定量角度来考察自然。在这方面，毕达哥拉斯学派的哲学家们无疑发挥了重要作用。
en: The earlier Ionian philosophers of nature had probably gone as far as they could to explain the workings of nature by means of speculative reason. These were truly great generalisations, which pointed in the right direction. But, in order to carry the process further, it was necessary to examine things in greater detail, to proceed to analyse nature piece by piece. This was later begun by Aristotle and the Alexandrine Greek thinkers. But an important part of this task was to consider nature from a quantitative point of view. Here the Pythagorean philosophers undoubtedly played a major role.

zh: 早在阿那克西美尼试图提出自然界中量与质的变化（稀化与凝聚）之间的关系这一问题时，就已经指向了这一方向。但这种方法到此时已达到极限，并已穷尽其可能性。正如J. D. 伯纳尔所言：
en: Already, Anaximenes had pointed in this direction in attempting to pose the question of the relation between changes of quantity and quality in nature (rarification and condensation). But this method had by now reached its limits and exhausted itself. As J. D. Bernal puts it:

zh: 爱奥尼亚学派的成就在于，它勾勒出一幅关于宇宙如何形成以及如何运行的图景，其中既没有神的干预，也没有预先的设计。其根本缺陷在于其模糊性和定性特征。仅靠它本身，无法取得进一步进展，也无法做出任何具体成果。当时所需要的，是将数字和数量引入哲学。
en: The triumph of the Ionian school was that it had set up a picture of how the universe had come into being and how it worked without the intervention of gods or design. Its basic weakness was its vagueness and qualitative character. By itself it could lead nowhere; nothing concrete could be done with it. What was needed was the introduction of number and quantity into philosophy.

zh: 从唯物主义到唯心主义
en: FROM MATERIALISM TO IDEALISM

zh: 古希腊哲学兴盛的时期，正值社会面临深刻危机，人们普遍对包括既定宗教在内的旧有信仰提出质疑。宗教信仰的危机催生了无神论倾向，并催生了基于唯物主义的真正科学世界观。然而，正如社会中一贯如此，这一过程是以矛盾的方式展开的。在理性主义和科学倾向的同时，我们也看到了与其相反的趋势——神秘主义和非理性思潮日益高涨。在罗马社会危机时期，曾发生过非常相似的现象，东方宗教迅速传播，而基督教最初只是其中之一。
en: The period of the ascent of ancient Greek philosophy was characterised by a profound crisis of society, marked by a general questioning of the old beliefs, including the established religion. The crisis of religious belief gave rise to atheist tendencies and the birth of a genuinely scientific outlook, based on materialism. However, as always in society, the process took place in a contradictory way. Alongside the rationalist and scientific tendencies, we also see the opposite – a growing trend towards mysticism and irrationality. A very similar phenomenon occurred at the time of the crisis of Roman society, with the rapid spread of oriental religions, of which Christianity was originally only one among many.

zh: 对于生活在社会危机时期的广大农民和奴隶来说，奥林匹斯山的众神显得遥不可及。这是一种属于上层阶级的宗教。在来世，他们无法指望因现世的苦难而获得未来的回报。希腊的冥界是一个由迷失灵魂栖居的阴郁之地。而新兴的宗教崇拜，凭借其模仿性的舞蹈和合唱（希腊悲剧的真正起源）、神秘仪式（源自动词myo，意为“守口如瓶”），以及对死后生命的承诺，对大众而言要吸引人得多。其中尤为流行的是酒神狄俄尼索斯（罗马人称之为巴克斯）的崇拜，其仪式包含酩酊大醉的狂欢。这比奥林匹斯的旧神要吸引人得多。
en: To the mass of peasants and slaves, living in a time of social crisis, the gods of Olympus seemed remote. This was a religion for the upper classes. There was no prospect of a future reward for present suffering in the afterlife. The Greek underworld was a cheerless place inhabited by lost souls. The newer cults, with their mimetic dancing and choral singing (the real origin of Greek tragedy), their mysteries (from the verb myo, meaning to keep your mouth shut), and the promise of life after death, was far more attractive to the masses. Particularly popular was the cult of Dionysius, the god of wine (known to the Romans as Bacchus), which involved drunken orgies. This was much more appealing than the old gods of Olympia.

zh: 正如罗马帝国衰落时期，以及当今资本主义衰落时期一样，各种神秘教派开始蔓延，其中掺杂了从色雷斯、小亚细亚乃至可能来自埃及的异域新仪式。其中尤为重要的是奥尔甫斯教派，该教派是狄俄尼索斯教派的进一步发展，与毕达哥拉斯学派有许多共同点。与毕达哥拉斯学派一样，奥尔甫斯教派的信徒相信灵魂转世。他们有净化仪式，包括禁食肉类，但用于圣礼的除外。他们对人的看法基于二元论——即身体与灵魂分离的观念。在他们看来，人一部分属于天，一部分属于地。
en: As in the period of decline of the Roman Empire, and in the present period of capitalist decline, there was a spread of all kinds of mystery cults, mixed with new exotic rites imported from Thrace and Asia Minor and possibly Egypt. Of particular importance was the cult of Orpheus, a refinement of the cult of Dionysius, with many points in common with the Pythagorean movement. Like the Pythagoreans, the followers of the cult of Orpheus believed in the transmigration of souls. They had rites of purification, including abstaining from meat, except for sacramental purposes. Their view of man was based on dualism – the idea of the cleavage of body and soul. For them, man was partly of heaven, partly of earth.

zh: 这些思想与毕达哥拉斯学派的教义如此接近，以至于一些学者（如伯里）认为，毕达哥拉斯学派实际上是奥尔甫斯运动的一个分支。这种说法有些夸大其词。尽管带有神秘主义色彩，毕达哥拉斯学派仍为人类思想的发展，尤其是数学领域，做出了重要贡献。它不能被简单地归类为一个宗教派别。尽管如此，我们不得不承认，毕达哥拉斯主义的唯心主义观念不仅是对宗教世界观的回响，而且直接源于宗教世界观。伯特兰·罗素将唯心主义的发展追溯到奥尔甫斯宗教的神秘主义：
en: So close are these ideas to the Pythagorean doctrines that some authors, such as Bury, maintain that the Pythagoreans were really a branch of the Orphean movement. This is an exaggeration. Despite its mystical elements, the Pythagorean school made an important contribution to the development of human thought, especially mathematics. It cannot be dismissed as a religious sect. Nevertheless, it is impossible to resist the conclusion that the idealist conceptions of Pythagoreanism are not just an echo of a religious world outlook, but stem directly from it. Bertrand Russell traces the development of idealism back to the mysticism of the Orphean religion:

zh: 这种神秘主义元素是随着毕达哥拉斯进入希腊哲学的，他正如奥尔甫斯是狄俄尼索斯宗教的改革者一样，是奥尔甫斯教的改革者。从毕达哥拉斯那里，奥尔甫斯教的元素进入了柏拉图的哲学，又从柏拉图那里传入了后来大多数在某种程度上带有宗教色彩的哲学。
en: This mystical element entered into Greek philosophy with Pythagoras, who was a reformer of Orphism as Orpheus was a reformer of the religion of Dionysius. From Pythagoras Orphic elements entered into the philosophy of Plato, and from Plato into most later philosophy that was in any degree religious.

zh: 随着奴隶制的扩张，脑力劳动与体力劳动之间的划分达到了极致的表现。这一现象与奥尔甫斯教的传播直接相关。奴隶制是异化的极端形式。在资本主义制度下，“自由”的劳动者与其劳动力相异化，劳动力对他而言呈现为一种独立且敌对的力量——资本。然而在奴隶制下，奴隶甚至丧失了作为人的存在本身。他什么也不是。他不是一个人，而只是一个“会说话的工具”。他劳动的产物、他的身体、他的思想、他的灵魂都属于他人，而那人会不顾他的意愿随意处置这些。奴隶未得到满足的欲望，以及他对世界和自身的极度异化，催生出对世界及其一切造物的排斥感。物质世界是邪恶的。生活是一片眼泪之谷。幸福无法在那里找到，唯有死亡才能带来解脱，使人从劳苦中解脱出来。灵魂一旦从肉体的牢笼中解放出来，便能获得自由。
en: The division between mental and manual labour reaches an extreme expression with the growth of slavery. This phenomenon was directly related to the spread of Orphism. Slavery is an extreme form of alienation. Under capitalism, the ‘free’ worker is alienated from his labour-power, which presents itself to him as a separate and hostile force – capital. Under slavery, however, the slave loses his very existence as a human being. He is nothing. Not a person, but a ‘tool with a voice’. The product of his labour, his body, his mind, his soul are the property of another, who disposes of them without regard to his wishes. The unfulfilled desires of the slave, his extreme alienation from the world and himself, gives rise to a feeling of rejection towards the world and all its works. The material world is evil. Life is a vale of tears. Happiness is not to be found there, only in death, which gives release from toil. The soul, freed from its prison in the body, can become free.

zh: 在社会衰落的所有时期，人们都有两种选择：要么直面现实，为改变它而奋斗；要么认定无路可走，并顺从命运。这两种截然不同的世界观不可避免地体现在两种对立的哲学之中——唯物主义与唯心主义。如果我们渴望改变世界，就必须理解它。我们必须直面现实。早期希腊唯物主义者那欢快的乐观主义正是这种态度的典型体现。他们渴望求知。后来，这一切都发生了变化。旧秩序的瓦解、奴隶制的兴起以及普遍的不安全感，导致了某种向内退缩与悲观的倾向。在缺乏明确替代方案的情况下，逃避现实、在神秘主义中寻求个人救赎的倾向逐渐占据上风。下层民众投身于神秘教派，例如谷物之神得墨忒尔、葡萄酒之神狄俄尼索斯，以及后来的奥尔甫斯教派。但上层阶级也未能免于这一时期的困境。那是动荡不安的时代。繁荣的城市可能在一夜之间化为灰烬，其市民或被杀害，或被卖为奴隶。
en: In all periods of social decline, men and women have two options: either to confront reality, and fight to change it, or to accept that there is no way out, and resign themselves to their fate. These two contrasting outlooks are inevitably reflected in two antagonistic philosophies – materialism and idealism. If we desire to change the world, it is necessary to understand it. We must look reality in the face. The cheerful optimism of the early Greek materialists was typical of this outlook. They wanted to know. Later, all that changed. The break-up of the old order, the rise of slavery and a general sense of insecurity led to a certain introversion and pessimism. In the absence of a clear alternative, the tendency to look away from reality, to seek individual salvation in mysticism, gradually gained ground. The lower orders looked to mystery cults, like those of Demeter, giver of corn, Dionysius, giver of wine, and later the cult of Orpheus. But the upper classes were not immune to the problems of the period. These were troubled times. Prosperous cities could be turned to ashes overnight, and their citizens killed or sold into slavery.

zh: 克罗通强大的商业竞争对手西巴里斯城，以其财富和奢华而闻名。上层阶级如此富庶，以至于关于“西巴里斯式”生活方式的各种离奇传说不绝于耳。一个典型的例子是，一位年轻的西巴里斯人起床时，竟抱怨床上有片皱巴巴的玫瑰叶。据说他们甚至用管道将葡萄酒输送到码头。尽管其中难免有些夸张，但显然这是一座极其繁荣的城市，富人过着极尽奢华的生活。然而，不平等现象的加剧引发了激烈的阶级斗争。
en: The city of Sybaris, Croton’s powerful commercial rival, was renowned for its wealth and luxury. So wealthy were the upper class that all kinds of tall stories were told about the ‘Sybarite’ lifestyle. A typical example was the young Sybarite who, upon rising, complained of a crumpled rose-leaf in his bed. It is said that they piped their wine to the quay. Allowing for an element of exaggeration, it is clear that this was a most prosperous city, where the rich lived a life of great luxury. However, the growth of inequality gave rise to a ferocious class struggle.

zh: 这一时期，劳动分工极度加剧，伴随着奴隶制的迅速扩张，贫富差距日益扩大。工业区与居民区完全隔离。但高墙与守卫并未能拯救西巴里斯的富人。与其他城邦一样，一场革命爆发了，其中“僭主”泰利斯在民众的支持下夺取了政权。这给了克罗通一个借口，使其得以向因内部分裂而实力削弱的宿敌宣战。经过七十天的战役，这座城市落入了克罗通之手。A. R. 伯恩评论道：
en: This was a period in which the division of labour was enormously intensified, accompanied by the rapid growth of slavery, and an ever-increasing gulf between rich and poor. The industrial and residential quarters were completely segregated. But high walls and guards did not save the rich citizens of Sybaris. As in other city states, a revolution erupted in which the ‘tyrant’, Telys, seized power with the support of the masses. This gave Croton the excuse to declare war on its rival, at a moment when it was weakened by internal divisions. After a seventy-day campaign, the city fell into their hands. A. R. Burn comments:

zh: 他们将城市彻底摧毁，将当地河流改道，使其流经城址，而幸存者则四散逃亡，大多前往西海岸。若将这场战争视为一场阶级战争，其特别的残暴性便更易理解。
en: They utterly destroyed it, turning the local river across its site, while survivors scattered, largely to the west coast. The particular savagery of this war is more easily understood when it is seen as a class war.

zh: 我们必须在这个特定的背景下看待毕达哥拉斯学派的兴起。正如罗马帝国衰落时期一样，统治阶级中的一部分人充满了焦虑、恐惧和困惑。无论是富人还是穷人，旧神都无法给予他们任何慰藉或解脱的希望。对于那些感觉自己正站在深渊边缘的人们来说，就连生活中的美好事物也失去了部分吸引力。在这种普遍不安全的环境下，即便是最强大、最繁荣的国家也可能在短时间内被推翻，毕达哥拉斯学说尽管具有苦行主义的特征——或者正因如此——却引起了统治阶级中一部分人的共鸣。这一运动的秘传性和智性特征使它无法吸引大众——而奥尔甫斯教派却在大众中赢得了庞大的追随者。
en: It is in this specific context that we must see the rise of the Pythagorean school of philosophy. As in the period of decline of the Roman Empire, a section of the ruling class was filled with a feeling of anxiety, fear and perplexity. The old gods offered no solace or hope of delivery, either to rich or poor. Even the good things in life lost some of their appeal to men and women who felt they were sitting on the edge of an abyss. Under such conditions of general insecurity, when even the strongest and most prosperous states could be overthrown in a short time, the doctrines of Pythagoras struck a chord with a section of the ruling class, despite their ascetic character, or even because of it. The esoteric and intellectual nature of this movement gave it no appeal to the masses, where the Orphic cult had gained a huge following.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯及其学派
en: PYTHAGORAS AND HIS SCHOOL

zh: 与其谈论其创始人，不如谈论该学派更为稳妥，因为很难将毕达哥拉斯的哲学思想与追随者的神话和蒙昧主义区分开来。他的著作没有留下任何残篇，甚至这些文字是否曾经存在都值得怀疑。就连毕达哥拉斯本人的存在也曾遭到质疑。然而，他的学派对希腊思想的影响是深远的。
en: It is safer to speak of the school rather than of its founder, since it is difficult to disentangle the philosophy of Pythagoras from the myths and obscurantism of his followers. No written fragments of his have survived, and it is doubtful if they ever existed. Even the existence of Pythagoras has been questioned. However, the influence of his school on Greek thought was profound.

zh: 据说毕达哥拉斯出生于萨摩斯岛，该岛与米利都一样，是一个繁荣的商业强国。当地的独裁者（“僭主”）波利克拉特斯推翻了土地贵族，并在商人阶级的支持下执政。历史学家希罗多德记载，他曾不分青红皂白地掠夺所有人的财产，因为他声称，如果他把财产归还给朋友，朋友会比他从未拿走时更加感激！据称，毕达哥拉斯年轻时曾在波利克拉特斯的庇护下作为一名“爱智慧者”（philo-sophos）活动。他曾前往腓尼基和埃及，据说在那里被接纳为埃及祭司阶层的一员。公元前530 年，为躲避内乱以及波斯人对爱奥尼亚的威胁，他逃往意大利南部的克罗通。
en: Pythagoras is said to have been a native of the island of Samos, a thriving commercial power, like Miletus. Its local dictator (‘tyrant’), Polycrates, had overthrown the landed aristocracy and was ruling with the support of the merchant class. Of him, the historian Herodotos reports that he robbed all men indiscriminately, for he said that his friends were more grateful if he gave them their property back than they would have been if he had never taken it! In his youth, Pythagoras apparently worked as a philo-sophos (lover of wisdom) under the patronage of Polycrates. He travelled to Phoenicia and Egypt, where he is said to have been initiated into an Egyptian priest caste. In 530 BC, he fled to Croton in southern Italy to escape from civil strife and the threat posed by the Persians to Ionia.

zh: 由于神话与传说层层叠加，几乎无法对这个人做出任何确切的论断。他的学派无疑是数学与科学探索以及宗教修道派别的一种非凡融合。该团体按照修道院模式运作，并设有严格的戒律，例如：不吃豆类；不捡拾掉落之物；不用铁器拨动火堆；不跨过撬棍等。其核心理念在于超脱尘世，通过基于数学的宁静沉思来寻求救赎——数学被赋予了所谓的神秘特质。可能受东方思想影响，毕达哥拉斯学派还宣扬灵魂转世说。
en: The luxuriant overgrowth of myth and fable makes it almost impossible to say anything certain about the man. His school certainly was a remarkable mixture of mathematical and scientific investigation and a religious-monastic sect. The community was run on monastic lines, with strict rules which included, for instance: not to eat beans; not to pick up what was fallen; not to stir the fire with iron; not to step over a crowbar, etc. The whole idea was to escape from the world, to seek salvation in a life of peaceful contemplation based on mathematics, which was invested with supposedly mystical qualities. Probably reflecting oriental influences, the Pythagoreans also preached the transmigration of souls.

zh: 与爱奥尼亚唯物主义者那种欢快世俗的态度形成鲜明对比的是，这里已经具备了后来由柏拉图发展出来、并被基督教所继承的未来唯心主义世界观的所有要素——这种世界观在随后的许多个世纪里，一直阻碍着科学探究精神的成长。J. 伯内特用以下文字精辟地表达了这种意识形态背后的核心思想：
en: In contrast to the cheerful worldliness of the Ionian materialists, here we have all the elements of the future idealist world outlook later developed by Plato, and taken over by Christianity, which bedevilled the growth of the spirit of scientific inquiry for many centuries. The moving spirit behind this ideology is aptly expressed by J. Burnet in the following lines:

zh: 我们是这个世界的过客，肉体是灵魂的坟墓，然而我们绝不能通过自杀来寻求解脱；因为我们是上帝的产业，他是我们的牧人，若无他的命令，我们无权逃离。在这世上，有三类人，正如参加奥林匹克运动会的人也有三类。最低等的是来买卖的，次等的是来参赛的。然而，最优秀的是那些仅仅来观赛的人。因此，最伟大的净化莫过于不涉利害的科学研究，而那些致力于此的人——真正的哲学家——才最有效地从“轮回”中解脱出来。
en: We are strangers in this world, and the body is the tomb of the soul, and yet we must not seek to escape by self-murder; for we are the chattels of God who is our herdsman, and without His command we have no right to make our escape. In this life, there are three kinds of men, just as there are three sorts of people who come to the Olympic Games. The lowest class is made up of those who come to buy and sell, the next above them are those who come to compete. Best of all, however, are those who come simply to look on. The greatest purification of all is, therefore, disinterested science, and it is the man who devotes himself to that, the true philosopher, who has most effectually released himself from the ‘wheel of birth’.

zh: 这种哲学带有浓厚的精英主义和修道院色彩，在克罗通的富裕阶层中颇受欢迎，尽管究竟有多少人真的放弃了吃豆子或其他食物，恐怕值得怀疑！这一切的共同点在于将灵魂与身体的彻底分离。这一思想源于史前时期关于人类在自然界中地位的观念，在历史上以不同形式流传至今。它甚至在希波克拉底的一部论著中再次出现：
en: This philosophy, with its strong elitist and monastic overtones, proved popular with the wealthy classes of Croton, although how many really gave up eating beans, or anything else, may be open to doubt! The common thread in all this is the radical separation of the soul from the body. This idea, with its roots in a prehistoric conception of man’s place in nature, has been passed down in different forms throughout history. It even resurfaces in one of the Hippocratic treatises:

zh: 当身体清醒时，灵魂并不受自身控制，而是分裂为多个部分，每个部分都专司某种特殊的身体功能，如听觉、视觉、触觉、运动以及身体的各种动作。但当身体处于静止状态时，灵魂便被唤醒并苏醒，成为自己的主人，并亲自执行身体的所有功能。当身体入睡时，它不会产生任何感觉，但此时醒着的灵魂却能感知一切；它看见可见之物，听见可闻之声，行走、触摸、感受疼痛并进行思考。简而言之，在睡眠期间，灵魂履行着身体与灵魂的所有功能。能正确理解这些事物，便意味着具有相当的智慧。
en: While the body is awake, the soul is not under its own control, but is split into various portions each being devoted to some special bodily function such as hearing, vision, touch, locomotion and all the various actions of the body. But when the body is at rest, the soul is stirred and roused and becomes its own master, and itself performs all the functions of the body. When the body is sleeping it receives no sensations, but the soul being awake at that time perceives everything; it sees what is visible, it hears what is audible, it walks, it touches, it feels pain and thinks. In short, during sleep the soul performs all the functions of both body and soul. A correct appreciation of these things implies considerable wisdom.

zh: 与那些刻意背离宗教和神话的爱奥尼亚唯物主义哲学家不同，毕达哥拉斯学派继承了奥尔甫斯秘仪教派的观念，即灵魂可以通过“出神”（ekstasis 一词意为“步出”）来摆脱躯体的束缚。只有当灵魂脱离了躯体的牢笼，才被认为能够展现其真实本性。死亡即是生命，生命即是死亡。因此，从其诞生之初，哲学唯心主义就与其孪生兄弟——宗教——一样，颠倒了思想与存在、人与自然、人与万物之间的真实关系。这种唯心主义以各种形式延续至今，带来了极其恶劣的后果。
en: In contrast to the Ionian materialist philosophers, who deliberately turned their backs on religion and mythology, the Pythagoreans took over the idea of the Orphic mystery cult, that the soul could free itself from the body by means of an ‘ecstasy’ (the word ekstasis means ‘stepping out’). Only when the soul left the prison of the body was it deemed to express its true nature. Death was life and life was death. Thus, from its inception, philosophical idealism, in common with its conjoined twin, religion, represented an inversion of the real relation between thought and being, man and nature, people and things. Such idealism has persisted down to the present time, in one form or another, with the most pernicious results.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学说
en: THE PYTHAGOREAN DOCTRINE

zh: 尽管毕达哥拉斯学说具有神秘主义色彩，但它在哲学发展史上仍标志着向前迈出了一步。这并不奇怪。在人类思想的演进过程中，有许多例子表明，对非理性且不科学目标的追求，反而推动了科学事业的发展。几个世纪以来，炼金术士们为寻找“哲学家之石”而徒劳地努力，最终以失败告终。但在这一过程中，他们在实验领域取得了极其重要的发现，这些发现为现代科学——尤其是化学——日后的发展奠定了基础。
en: In spite of its mystical character, the Pythagorean doctrine marked a step forward in the development of philosophy. There is nothing strange about this. In the evolution of human thought, there are many instances in which the pursuit of irrational and unscientific goals nevertheless have furthered the cause of science.
