For centuries, the alchemists exerted themselves fruitlessly in an attempt to discover the ‘philosopher’s stone’. This ended in failure. But in the process, they made extremely important discoveries in the field of experiment which provided the basis upon which modern science, especially chemistry, later developed.

zh: 爱奥尼亚哲学的基本倾向是试图从现实世界的经验中进行概括。毕达哥拉斯及其追随者则试图通过另一条途径来理解事物的本质。施韦格勒对此这样阐述：
en: The basic tendency of Ionian philosophy was an attempt to generalise from the experience of the real world. Pythagoras and his followers attempted to arrive at an understanding of the nature of things by a different route. Schwegler puts it thus:

zh: 我们同样进行抽象，但处于更高的阶段：当人们不再关注一般物质的感性具体形态；当注意力不再聚焦于物质的质的方面——如水、空气等——而是转向其量的尺度与关系；当思考不再指向物质本身，而是指向事物在空间中存在的形式与秩序。
en: We have the same abstraction, but on a higher stage, when the sensuous concretion of matter in general is looked away from; when attention is turned no longer to the qualitative aspect of matter, as water, air, etc., but to its quantitative measure and relations; when reflection is directed, not to the material, but to the form and order of things as they exist in space.

zh: 人类思想的总体进步与从现实中进行抽象的能力密切相关，即能够从众多特殊事例中得出普遍结论。由于现实是多方面的，因此可以以多种不同的方式来诠释它，从而反映真理的这一或那一要素。我们在哲学史上屡见不鲜：伟大的思想家抓住现实的一个方面，将其奉为绝对且最终的真理，却被下一代思想家所推翻，而后者又重复这一过程。然而，各大哲学流派和科学理论的兴衰，恰恰体现了人类思想通过无休止的连续逼近过程而发展与丰富。
en: The progress of human thought in general is closely linked to the capacity to make abstractions from reality, to be able to draw general conclusions from a host of particulars. Since reality is many-sided, it is possible to interpret it in many different ways, reflecting this or that element of the truth. This we see many times in the history of philosophy, where great thinkers laid hold of one aspect of reality, and held it up as an absolute and final truth, only to be swept away by the next generation of thinkers, who in turn repeat the process. Yet the rise and fall of great philosophical schools and scientific theories represents the development and enrichment of human thought by a process of endless successive approximations.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派从数字和数量关系的角度来理解世界。对毕达哥拉斯而言，万物皆为数字。这一思想与对宇宙内在和谐的探索密切相关。他们认为数字是万物发展的源头。尽管其中带有神秘主义色彩，但他们仍取得了重要发现，极大地推动了数学——尤其是几何学——的发展。他们创造了“奇数”和“偶数”这两个术语，认为奇数代表男性，偶数代表女性。由于该团体不允许女性加入，他们自然将奇数视为神圣，而将偶数视为世俗！同样，我们所说的“平方”和“立方”这两个术语也源自毕达哥拉斯学派，他们还发现了音阶中的调和数列，将琴弦的长度与其振动音高的关系联系起来。
en: The Pythagoreans approached the world from the standpoint of number and quantity relations. For Pythagoras, all things are numbers. This idea was linked to the search for the underlying harmony of the universe. They believed that number was the element out of which all things developed. Despite the mystical element, they made important discoveries which greatly stimulated the development of mathematics, especially geometry. They invented the terms odd and even numbers, odd numbers being male and even ones female. Since no women were allowed in the community, they naturally declared odd numbers to be divine and even ones earthly! Likewise, our terms squares and cubes of numbers come from the Pythagoreans, who also discovered harmonic progression in the musical scale, linking the length of a string and the pitch of its vibrating note.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派并未将这些重要发现应用于任何实际用途，他们纯粹从抽象的神秘主义角度对几何学感兴趣。然而，这些发现对后世的思想产生了决定性的影响。数学作为一门深奥学科、普通凡人难以企及的神秘色彩，一直延续至今。这种观念通过柏拉图的唯心主义哲学得以传承，他在学园入口处刻下了这样的铭文：“凡不懂几何者，不得入内。”
en: These important discoveries were not put to any practical use by the Pythagoreans, who were interested in geometry purely from an abstract mystical point of view. Yet they had a determining influence on subsequent thought. The mystique of mathematics as an esoteric subject, inaccessible to ordinary mortals, has persisted down to the present day. It was transmitted through the idealist philosophy of Plato, who placed over the entrance of his school the inscription: “Let no man destitute of geometry enter my doors.”

zh: 法林顿教授写道：
en: Professor Farrington writes:

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派的宇宙观既奇特又重要。他们不像爱奥尼亚学派那样，试图通过某些物质元素和物理过程的行为来描述宇宙，而是完全通过数字来描述宇宙。很久以后，亚里士多德曾指出，他们将数字视为宇宙的质料与形式。数字构成了他们世界所由之成的实际物质。他们将点称为“一”，线称为“二”，面称为“三”，立体称为“四”，这依据的是定义这四种维度所需的最小点数。
en: The cosmology of the Pythagoreans is very curious and very important. They did not, like the Ionians, try to describe the universe in terms of the behaviour of certain material elements and physical processes. They described it exclusively in terms of number. Aristotle said long afterwards that they took number to be the matter as well as the form of the universe. Numbers constituted the actual stuff of which their world was made. They called a point One, a line Two, a surface Three, a solid Four, according to the minimum number of points necessary to define each of these dimensions.

zh: 他们赋予特定数字——三、四、七——以神奇的意义。其中，数字十尤为重要，它是1、2、3 和4 的总和。这些迷信观念至今仍存在于圣三位一体、启示录中的四骑士、七宗罪等概念中。“同样明显的是，”伯纳尔补充道，“在现代数学物理学中，每当其行家试图将上帝塑造成至高无上的数学家时，这种倾向便显露无遗。”
en: They attached magical significance to particular numbers – three, four, seven. Of particular significance was the number ten, which is the sum of one, two, three and four. These superstitions still persist in the Holy Trinity, the four horsemen of the Apocalypse, the seven deadly sins, and the like. “It is also apparent”, adds Bernal, “in modern mathematical physics whenever its adepts try to make God the supreme mathematician.”

zh: 科学史的特点在于，人们为捍卫特定的思想学派而表现出极其强烈的派别立场，有时甚至近乎狂热。这些学派自诩为绝对真理的捍卫者，实际上确实体现了人类知识在特定时间点所达到的最高水平。只有科学本身的进一步发展，才能揭示特定理论的局限性和内在矛盾，该理论随后会被其对立面所否定，而对立面又会被进一步否定，如此循环往复，无穷无尽。这一过程正是科学史的辩证法，几个世纪以来，它始终与哲学史并行发展，起初几乎难以区分。
en: The history of science is characterised by the most fierce partisanship, at times bordering on fanaticism, in defence of particular schools of thought, which put themselves forward as the protagonists of an absolute truth, and who do in fact embody the maximum point reached by human knowledge at a given point in time. Only the further development of science itself reveals the limitations and inner contradictions of a given theory, which is then negated by its opposite, which is itself negated, and so on ad infinitum. This process is precisely the dialectic of the history of science, which for centuries proceeded in tandem with the history of philosophy, and initially was virtually indistinguishable from it.

zh: “万物皆数”
en: ‘ALL THINGS ARE NUMBERS’

zh: 自然研究中定量方面的发展显然具有至关重要的意义。没有它，科学将停留在单纯的一般性层面，无法进一步发展。然而，当这样的突破发生时，人们不可避免地会倾向于对其做出夸大的断言。在这里所讨论的科学仍与宗教纠缠不清的情形中，这一点尤为明显。
en: The development of the quantitative side of investigating nature was obviously of crucial importance. Without it, science would have remained on the level of mere generalities, incapable of further development. However, when such a breakthrough takes place, there is inevitably a tendency to make exaggerated claims on its behalf. This is particularly true in this case, where science is still entangled with religion.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派将数——即数量关系——视为万物的本质：万物皆为数。的确，许多自然现象都可以用数学来解释。然而，即便是最先进的数学模型，也只是对现实世界的近似描述。然而，纯粹定量方法的局限性早在很久以前就已显而易见。黑格尔作为一位坚定的唯心主义者和杰出的数学家，本应对毕达哥拉斯学派充满热情。然而，事实却远非如此。黑格尔对“世界可以归结为定量关系”这一观点嗤之以鼻。
en: The Pythagoreans saw number – quantitative relations – as the essence of all things: all things are numbers. Indeed, it is possible to explain many natural phenomena in mathematical terms. Nevertheless, even the most advanced mathematical models are only approximations of the real world. The inadequacy of the purely quantitative approach, however, was evident long ago. Hegel, who was a convinced idealist and a formidable mathematician, might have been expected to be enthusiastic about the Pythagorean school. However, this was far from the case. Hegel poured scorn on the idea that the world could be reduced to quantitative relations.

zh: 从毕达哥拉斯开始，人们就以数学的名义提出了最夸张的主张，将数学描绘成“科学的女王”，是开启宇宙所有大门的神奇钥匙。数学摆脱了与粗糙物质现实的一切联系，仿佛飞升至天界，在那里获得了神一般的存在，只遵循自身法则。因此，二十世纪初，伟大的数学家亨利·庞加莱曾断言，科学定律与现实世界毫无关联，而是任意约定，旨在对相应现象作出更便捷、更“有用”的描述。如今许多物理学家公开宣称，其数学模型的有效性并不取决于经验验证，而是取决于方程的美学品质。
en: From Pythagoras onwards, the most extravagant claims have been made on behalf of mathematics, which has been portrayed as the queen of the sciences, the magic key opening all doors of the universe. Breaking free from all contact with crude material reality, mathematics appeared to soar into the heavens, where it acquired a god-like existence, obeying no rule but its own. Thus, the great mathematician Henri Poincaré, in the early years of the twentieth century, could claim that the laws of science did not relate to the real world at all, but represented arbitrary conventions destined to promote a more convenient and ‘useful’ description of the corresponding phenomena. Many physicists now openly state that the validity of their mathematical models does not depend upon empirical verification, but on the aesthetic qualities of their equations.

zh: 因此，数学理论一方面是巨大科学进步的源泉，另一方面却也是众多错误和误解的根源，这些错误和误解曾带来、且至今仍在带来深远的负面影响。其核心错误在于试图将自然界复杂、动态且充满矛盾的运作归结为静态、有序的定量公式。从毕达哥拉斯学派开始，自然就被以形式主义的方式呈现为一维的点，进而演变为线、面、立方体、球体等等。乍看之下，纯数学的世界是一个绝对思想的世界，未受物质接触的玷污。但正如恩格斯指出的那样，这与事实相去甚远。我们使用十进制，并非源于逻辑推导或“自由意志”，而是因为我们有十根手指。“数字”（digital）一词就源自拉丁语中表示“手指”的词。时至今日，一个小学生在求解抽象的数学题之前，仍会在实体的课桌下偷偷数着自己实体的手指。通过这种方式，孩子在无意识中重现了早期人类学习计数的过程。
en: Thus, the theories of mathematics have been, on the one side, the source of tremendous scientific advance and, on the other, the origin of numerous errors and misconceptions which have had, and are still having, profoundly negative consequences. The central error is to attempt to reduce the complex, dynamic and contradictory workings of nature to static, orderly quantitative formulae. Starting with the Pythagoreans, nature is presented in a formalistic manner, as a single-dimensional point, which becomes a line, which becomes a plane, a cube, a sphere, and so on. At first sight, the world of pure mathematics is one of absolute thought, unsullied by contact with material things. But this is far from the truth, as Engels points out. We use the decimal system, not because of logical deduction or ‘free will’, but because we have ten fingers. The word ‘digital’ comes from the Latin word for fingers. And to this day, a schoolboy will secretly count his material fingers beneath a material desk, before arriving at the answer to an abstract mathematical problem. In so doing, the child is unconsciously retracing the way in which early humans learned to count.
body.review: 原文将点称为single-dimensional（一维的），这里照录；通常几何学中的点没有维度。

zh: 数学抽象概念的物质起源对亚里士多德来说并非秘密：
en: The material origins of the abstractions of mathematics were no secret to Aristotle:

zh: 数学家研究的是抽象概念。他剔除所有可感知的属性，如重量、密度、温度等，仅保留数量属性、连续性（一维、二维或三维）及其本质的属性。
en: The mathematician investigates abstractions. He eliminates all sensible qualities like weight, density, temperature, etc., leaving only the quantitative and continuous (in one, two or three dimensions) and its essential attributes.

zh: 在另一处，他指出：
en: Elsewhere, he says:

zh: 数学对象不能脱离可感（即物质）事物而独立存在。
en: Mathematical objects cannot exist apart from sensible (i.e. material) things.

zh: 我们没有经验到任何仅由线、面或点构成的东西，如果这些事物是物质实体的话，我们本应有这样的经验；线等概念在定义上或许先于物体，但并不因此就在实体上先于物体。
en: We have no experience of anything which consists of lines or planes or points, as we should have if these things were material substances, lines, etc., may be prior in definition to body, but they are not on that account prior in substance.

zh: 数学的发展源于人类非常现实的需求。早期人类起初只有十个数字发音，这正是因为他们像小孩子一样用手指计数。例外是中美洲的玛雅人，他们的计数系统基于二十进制而非十进制，这可能是因为他们不仅用手指，还用脚趾计数。早期人类生活在简单的狩猎采集社会中，没有货币也没有私有财产，因此不需要大数。要表达大于十的数，他们只需将与手指相关的十种发音进行组合即可。因此，比十大一的数用“一十”（拉丁语为undecim，早期日耳曼语为ein-lifon——“多出一”——即现代英语中的eleven）来表示。除“百”、“千”、“百万”、“十亿”和“万亿”这五个附加单位外，所有其他数字都只是这十种原始发音的组合。
en: The development of mathematics is the result of very material human needs. Early man at first had only ten number sounds, precisely because he counted, like a small child, on his fingers. The exception was the Mayas of Central America, who had a numerical system based on twenty instead of ten, probably because they counted their toes as well as their fingers. Early man, living in a simple hunter-gatherer society, without money or private property, had no need of large numbers. To convey a number larger than ten, he merely combined some of the ten sounds connected with his fingers. Thus, one more than ten is expressed by ‘one-ten’ (undecim, in Latin, or ein-lifon – ‘one over’ – in early Teutonic, which becomes eleven in modern English). All the other numbers are only combinations of the original ten sounds, with the exception of five additions – hundred, thousand, million, billion and trillion.

zh: 十七世纪伟大的英国唯物主义哲学家托马斯·霍布斯早已洞悉了数字的真正起源：
en: The real origin of numbers was already understood by the great English materialist philosopher of the seventeenth century, Thomas Hobbes:

zh: 似乎曾有一段时期，这些数字名称尚未被使用；人们不得不借助一只或两只手上的手指，来清点他们想要计数的事物；正因如此，如今在任何国家，数字词都只有十个，而在某些国家只有五个，之后又重新开始。
en: And it seems, there was a time when those names of number were not in use; and men were fayn to apply their fingers of one or both hands, to those things they desired to keep account of; and that thence it proceeded, that now our numerall words are but ten, in any Nation, and in some but five, and then they begin again.

zh: 阿尔弗雷德·胡珀解释道：
en: Alfred Hooper explains:

zh: 仅仅因为原始人发明的数字发音数量与他手指的数量相同，我们今天的数制才成为十进制，即以十为基础的数制，由前十个基本数字发音的无尽重复组成……如果人类被赋予十二根手指而不是十根，那么我们今天无疑会采用十二进制数制，即以十二为基础的数制，由十二个基本数字发音的无尽重复组成。
en: Just because primitive man invented the same number of number-sounds as he had fingers, our number-scale today is a decimal one, that is, a scale based on ten, and consisting of endless repetitions of the first ten basic number-sounds … Had men been given twelve fingers instead of ten, we should doubtless have a duo-decimal number-scale today, one based on twelve, consisting of endless repetitions of twelve basic number-sounds.

zh: 事实上，与十进制相比，十二进制具有某些优势。十只能被2 和5 整除，而十二则能被2、3、4 和6 整除。这一论点的证明可从古代苏美尔人的六十进制中找到，该体系将太阳年划分为十二个月、360 天，而我们现行的24 小时制和60 分钟制正是由此演变而来。最近对一块来自森克雷（今伊拉克境内）的、距今3,700 年的泥板的研究证明，古巴比伦人基于这一计数系统，早在希腊人之前1,000 多年就发展出了一种比我们更先进的三角学形式。
en: In fact, a duodecimal system has certain advantages in comparison to the decimal one. Whereas ten can only be exactly divided by two and five, twelve can be divided exactly by two, three, four and six. The proof of this can be found in the ancient Sumerian sexagesimal system, which produced a solar year of twelve months and 360 days, and from which we have taken our twenty-four-hour days and sixty minute hours. A recent study of a 3,700 year-old tablet from Senkereh, modern Iraq, has proven that the ancient Babylonians had developed a superior form of trigonometry to our own, over 1,000 years before the Greeks, on the basis of this system.

zh: 尽管古代苏美尔人并没有十二根手指，但人们仍认为，这一看似违反十进制规则的现象，其起源在于通过手指和脚趾进行计数——先数到二十，再数到四十，接着数到六十，然后循环往复。苏美尔楔形文字中的一至九，是手指的图示，这与罗马数字系统颇为相似——在罗马数字中，一至四代表手指，而五的符号很可能代表拇指与食指之间的缝隙。词汇“calculus”（英语calculate（计算）由此衍生）在拉丁语中意为“小石子”，与在算盘上数石珠的方法有关。这些以及无数其他例子都说明，数学并非源于人类思维的自由运作，而是社会演变、试错、观察和实验这一漫长过程的产物，最终逐渐分离出来，形成了一套看似抽象的知识体系。
en: But while the ancient Sumerians did not have twelve fingers, the origin of this seeming exception to the decimal rule is still thought to have been in the counting of fingers and toes, up to twenty, forty and then sixty before beginning the sequence again. Numbers one to nine in the Sumerian cuneiform script are pictorial representations of fingers, not unlike the Roman system, in which numbers one to four are representations of fingers, and the symbols for five likely represented the gap between thumb and index fingers. The word ‘calculus’ (from which we derive ‘calculate’) means ‘pebble’ in Latin, connected with the method of counting stone beads on an abacus. These and countless other examples serve to illustrate how mathematics did not arise from the free operation of the human mind, but is the product of a lengthy process of social evolution, trial and error, observation and experiment, which gradually becomes separated out as a body of knowledge of an apparently abstract character.

zh: 同样，我们现行的度量衡体系也源于物质对象。英语中的度量单位“英尺”（foot）的由来不言自明，西班牙语中表示“英寸”的词“pulgada”意为“拇指”，其由来亦然。最基本的数学符号+ 和− 的起源与数学毫无关系。它们是中世纪商人用来计算仓库中货物数量多余或短缺时所使用的标记。
en: Similarly, our present systems of weights and measures have been derived from material objects. The origin of the English unit of measurement, the foot, is self-evident, as is the Spanish word for an inch, pulgada, which means a thumb. The origin of the most basic mathematical symbols + and − has nothing to do with mathematics. They were the signs used in the Middle Ages by the merchants to calculate excess or deficiency of quantities of goods in warehouses.

zh: 为了建造住所以抵御自然环境的侵袭，早期人类不得不寻找最佳且最实用的木材切割方法，使木料两端能够紧密契合。这促成了直角和木工角尺的发现。在平地上建造房屋的需求，催生了埃及和罗马墓葬中描绘的那种水平仪——它由三块木头拼接成等腰三角形，顶点处系有一根绳子。金字塔的建造就使用了这类简单实用的工具。埃及祭司们积累了大量数学知识，这些知识最终都源于此类实践活动。
en: The need to build dwellings to protect themselves from the elements forced early man to find the best and most practical way of cutting wood so that their ends fitted closely together. This meant the discovery of the right angle and the carpenters’ square. The need to build a house on level ground led to the invention of the kind of levelling instrument depicted in Egyptian and Roman tombs, consisting of three pieces of wood joined together in an isosceles triangle, with a cord fastened at the apex. Such simple practical tools were used in the construction of the pyramids. The Egyptian priests accumulated a huge body of mathematical knowledge derived ultimately from such practical activity.

zh: “几何学”一词本身就揭示了其实践起源。它简单地意味着“大地测量”。希腊人的贡献在于为这些发现提供了完整的理论表述。然而，在将他们的定理呈现为纯粹的逻辑演绎产物时，他们误导了自己和后世。归根结底，数学源于物质现实，事实上，若非如此，数学便毫无应用价值。就连每个学生都熟知的著名毕达哥拉斯定理——即在直角三角形最长边上画的正方形面积等于另外两条边上所画正方形面积之和——其实早已被古埃及人通过实践推导出来。
en: The very word ‘geometry’ betrays its practical origins. It means simply ‘earth-measurement’. The virtue of the Greeks was to give a finished theoretical expression to these discoveries. However, in presenting their theorems as the pure product of logical deduction, they were misleading themselves and future generations. Ultimately, mathematics derives from material reality and, indeed, could have no application if this were not the case. Even the famous theorem of Pythagoras, known to every school pupil, that a square drawn on the longest side of a right triangle is equal to the sum of the squares drawn on the other two sides, had been already worked out in practice by the Egyptians.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派背离了试图基于现实世界经验进行概括的爱奥尼亚唯物主义传统，他们断言，数学中的更高真理无法从感性经验的世界中推导出来，而只能通过纯粹理性的演绎推导出来。哲学家从某些必须被视为真实的“第一原理”出发，仅使用公认的第一原理或由此推导出的事实，通过一系列逻辑推演，最终得出结论。这被称为“先验推理”，源自拉丁语中“源于最初”的短语。
en: The Pythagoreans, breaking with the Ionian materialist tradition which attempted to generalise on the basis of experience of the real world, asserted that the higher truths of mathematics could not be derived from the world of sensuous experience, but only from the workings of pure reason, by deduction. Beginning with certain first principles, which have to be taken as true, the philosopher argues them through a series of logical stages until he arrives at a conclusion, using only facts that are agreed first principles, or are derived from such. This was known as a priori reasoning, from the Latin phrase denoting ‘from what comes first’.

zh: 毕达哥拉斯学派利用演绎法和先验推理，试图建立一个基于完美形式、受神圣和谐支配的宇宙模型。问题在于，现实世界中的形式远非完美。例如，他们认为天体是沿完美圆周运动的完美球体。这对当时而言是一项革命性的进步，但这两项断言实际上都不属实。试图将完美的和谐强加于宇宙、使其摆脱矛盾的尝试，甚至在数学层面上也很快就破产了。内部矛盾开始浮出水面，这导致了毕达哥拉斯学派的危机。
en: Using deduction and a priori reasoning, the Pythagoreans attempted to establish a model of the universe based on perfect forms and governed by divine harmony. The problem is that the forms of the real world are anything but perfect. For instance, they thought that the heavenly bodies were perfect spheres moving in perfect circles. This was a revolutionary advance for its time, but neither of these assertions is really true. The attempt to impose a perfect harmony on the universe, to free it from contradiction, soon broke down even in mathematical terms. Internal contradictions began to surface which led to a crisis of the Pythagorean school.

zh: 大约在公元前五世纪中叶，梅塔庞图姆的希帕索斯发现，在正方形和正五边形等简单图形中，边与对角线之间的数量关系是不可通约的，也就是说，无论整数多大，都无法用整数比来表示。2 的平方根无法用任何数表示。事实上，这就是数学家所说的“无理数”。这一发现使整个理论陷入混乱。此前，毕达哥拉斯学派一直主张世界是由具有大小的点构成的。虽然可能无法确定一条给定直线上有多少个点，但人们仍假设其数量是有限的。如今，如果正方形的对角线与边长是不可通约的，那么由此可推断，直线是可以无限分割的，而构成宇宙的那些微小点并不存在。
en: About the middle of the fifth century, Hippius of Metapontum discovered that the quantitative relations between the side and the diagonal of simple figures like the square and the regular pentagon are incommensurable, that is, they cannot be expressed as a ratio of whole numbers, no matter how great. The square root of two cannot be expressed by any number. It is, in fact, what mathematicians call an ‘irrational’ number. This discovery threw the whole theory into confusion. Hitherto, the Pythagoreans had taught that the world was constructed out of points with magnitude. While it might not be possible to say how many points there were on a given line, still they were assumed to be finite in number. Now if the diagonal and the side of a square are incommensurable, it follows that lines are infinitely divisible, and that the little points from which the universe was built do not exist.

zh: 自那时起，毕达哥拉斯学派便走上了衰落之路。该学派分裂为两个对立的派别：其中一派沉溺于日益深奥的数学思辨之中，另一派则试图通过精妙的数学创新来化解这一矛盾，这些创新为定量科学的发展奠定了基础。
en: From that time on, the Pythagorean school entered into decline. It split into two rival factions, one of which buried itself in ever more abstruse mathematical speculation, while the other attempted to overcome the contradiction by means of ingenious mathematical innovations which laid the basis for the development of the quantitative sciences.
